The Ravens' outlook on offense is already tenuous, with Lamar Jackson's ankle injury preventing him from practicing Wednesday and threatening his availability for Sunday's game in Atlanta. Flowers still has time to ramp up to a full practice before the end of the week to put himself on a path to playing this weekend.

headline: Ravens head coach Jesse Minter said that Flowers (hamstring) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice, Brian Wacker of The Baltimore Sun reports.
story: Though Flowers wasn't present on the field for the media-access portion of practice, the fourth-year wideout was apparently able to get in some work behind the scenes Wednesday. The Ravens haven't indicated that Flowers has experienced any setbacks with his hamstring since returning from a one-game absence to play in both of the previous two contests, so his limitations to begin Week 5 prep were most likely maintenance-related. Flowers still appears likely to head into Sunday's game in Atlanta without an injury designation, though his fantasy appeal may be more limited than usual with Tyler Huntley trending toward drawing the Week 5 start in place of the injured Lamar Jackson (ankle).

headline: Flowers caught eight of 10 targets for 118 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 24-18 win over the Titans.
story: The fourth-year wideout didn't appear hampered by the minor hamstring issue he's been playing through, as he led the Ravens in catches, targets and receiving yards while connecting with Lamar Jackson (ankle) for a 19-yard score early in the second quarter. Jackson's day was done at halftime and he was seen in a walking boot after the game, but per Jonas Shaffer of TheBaltimoreBanner.com, coach Jesse Minter suggested the QB might have tried playing in the second half if it seemed necessary to preserve the win. If Tyler Huntley is under center in Week 5 against the Falcons instead of Jackson, it could impact Flowers' ability to produce big numbers again. In three games, Flowers has delivered an 18-352-2 line on just 22 targets.

headline: Flowers (hamstring) is listed as active Sunday against the Titans.
story: Flowers has been tending to a hamstring injury since before halftime of the Ravens' Week 1 win at Indianapolis, but he was able to play last Sunday versus the Cowboys in Brazil, recording a 5-84-0 line on six targets on a 33 percent snap share. Despite entering this weekend as questionable, he isn't expected to be on a "pitch count" Sunday, per Jeremy Fowler of ESPN, meaning a full workload is on tap for the fourth-year wide receiver.

headline: Flowers (hamstring) is expected to play in Sunday's game against the Titans, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
story: Flowers carried a questionable tag into the weekend due to a lingering hamstring issue, but he's slated to suit up in Week 4 for a second straight week. Last Sunday against the Cowboys in Brazil, he handled a 33 percent snap share and hauled in five of six targets for 84 yards, but per Jeremy Fowler of ESPN, Flowers isn't expected to be on a "pitch count" this Sunday, so he appears set for a full workload.

headline: Flowers (hamstring) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Titans after being limited in Friday's practice.
story: After upgrading to full participation Thursday, Flowers took a step back Friday, but it's possible the Ravens just rested him some considering the addition of "rest" alongside his name on the injury report, per Jonas Shaffer of TheBaltimoreBanner.com. Flowers is likely better than 50/50 to play Sunday against the Titans. He's a locked-in WR2 in fantasy with big-time upside when available.

headline: Flowers (hamstring) was a full participant at Thursday's practice, Jamison Hensley of ESPN.com reports.
story: After being limited Wednesday, Flowers upgraded to full participation Thursday, putting him on track to avoid an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Titans. The speedy wideout injured his hamstring in the season opener against the Colts and sat out the Week 2 loss to the Saints before returning for the Ravens' Week 3 win over the Cowboys in Rio de Janeiro. Despite missing a game, Flowers easily leads the team with 234 receiving yards.

headline: Flowers (hamstring) was limited in Wednesday's practice, Sam Cohn of The Baltimore Sun reports.
story: Baltimore is continuing to exercise caution with its star receiver, who is working his way back to 100 percent from a hamstring injury. Flowers was effective in his return Sunday but logged only 21 (33 percent) offensive snaps. He didn't aggravate the injury Sunday, though his practice reps remain limited for now.

headline: Head coach Jesse Minter said Monday that he expects Flowers to carry a full workload in Week 4 against the Titans on Sunday, Clifton Brown of the Ravens' official site reports.
story: Flowers had his workload limited during Sunday's 34-31 win against the Cowboys in Brazil. Despite playing only 21 snaps on offense, the fourth-year wide receiver finished with five catches on six targets for 84 yards to lead Ravens pass catchers in all three categories. Flowers will be Lamar Jackson's favorite target heading into Week 4 against a Titans defense that ranks eighth in the league in passing yards allowed per game (189.0).

headline: Flowers (hamstring) caught five of six targets for 84 yards and added a 20-yard rush in Sunday's 34-31 win over the Cowboys.
story: Flowers led the Ravens in catches, targets and receiving yards in his return following a one-game absence due to a hamstring injury. His most consequential catch was a 27-yard reception on the game's penultimate play, which set up Tyler Loop's game-winning 56-yard field goal. Per Jonas Shaffer of the Baltimore Banner, Flowers knew for a while that he would be suiting up Sunday, but he was limited in practice due to concerns about the quality of the field in Rio de Janeiro. Flowers has seemingly put the injury behind him heading into a Week 4 home game against the Titans.

headline: Flowers (hamstring) is active for Sunday's game against the Cowboys in Rio de Janeiro, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
story: Flowers' active status is a bit of a surprise considering he's logged just one limited practice since suffering a hamstring injury in the first half of a Week 1 win at Indianapolis. On top of that, the field conditions in Brazil appear to be less than ideal, but it won't stop the Ravens from making him available to handle snaps Sunday. How many plays that may translate to remains to be seen, but Flowers and Rashod Bateman presumably will be the top wide receivers at the disposal of QB Lamar Jackson.

headline: The Ravens continue to view Flowers (hamstring) as a game-time decision leading up to Sunday's tilt with the Cowboys in Rio de Janeiro, and the wide receiver is expected to be limited to "somewhere in the realm of 20 to 30 plays" if he suits up, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
story: After turning in a limited practice Friday, Flowers went through a pregame workout Sunday and appeared to be moving around well while testing out both his left hamstring and the soggy field conditions in Brazil. The Ravens are still contemplating whether to make Flowers available for the Week 3 contest, with an official call on his status expected to arrive when the team releases its inactive list 90 minutes prior to the 4:25 p.m. ET kickoff. Even if Flowers gets clearance to play, he looks like he could handle well under a full workload, making him a less appealing fantasy option than he normally would be as the Ravens' No. 1 wide receiver.

headline: Flowers (hamstring) "looked good" during a pregame workout, but he remains questionable for Sunday's game against the Cowboys in Rio de Janeiro, and the Ravens are still mulling whether he'll play, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
story: The field conditions in Brazil are a major factor in the Ravens' decision regarding the status of Flowers, who is nursing a hamstring injury and sat out the Week 2 loss to the Saints. He remained sidelined for the Ravens' first two Week 3 practices back in the United States before making the trip to Brazil and turning in a limited practice Friday. Flowers seemingly responded well both to that practice and during his pregame work, but he still looks to be a true game-time call leading up to the 4:25 p.m. ET kickoff. Even if Flowers gains clearance to play, the Ravens could manage his snaps to some degree.

headline: Flowers (hamstring) will participate in a pregame workout to determine his status for Sunday's game against the Cowboys in Rio de Janeiro, but the Ravens don't appear as if they expect him to play, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
story: Both Schefter and Ian Rapoport of NFL Network are calling Flowers a "true pregame decision," but the field conditions in Brazil ultimately appear to be a factor in whether or not the wide receiver will be cleared for game action, according to Mike Garafolo of NFL Network. Such a call won't be made by Baltimore until about 90 minutes before Sunday's 4:25 p.m. ET kickoff, but if Flowers ends up missing a second game in a row, Rashod Bateman will serve as the team's No. 1 wideout.

headline: Flowers (hamstring) is expected to "test his injury" prior to Sunday's game against the Cowboys, and if he suits up he "will likely be on a pitch count," Jeremy Fowler of ESPN.com reports.
story: Flowers was limited on Friday's injury report and given a questionable designation for Week 3, so the door is open for him to take the field Sunday in Brazil. However, it appears a final call on his availability will not be made until the Ravens release their inactives 90 minutes prior to Sunday's 4:25 p.m. ET kickoff, and even if Flowers is active he may not handle a full complement of snaps. Rashod Bateman would be the favorite to pick up the slack if Flowers is limited or unavailable altogether.

headline: Flowers (hamstring) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Cowboys in Brazil.
story: Flowers upgraded to limited practice participation Friday after sitting out every other session the past two weeks. It's unclear if he has a real chance to play, or if the Ravens are just trying to create that impression, so fantasy managers will need to stay tuned as the 4:25 p.m. ET kickoff approaches Sunday. It'll be a tricky situation if Flowers comes down to a game-time call, but there are at least three other games with late-afternoon kickoffs, plus SNF and MNF. Flowers' teammate Rashod Bateman is one of the better replacement options after putting up 88 yards and a TD in Flowers' absence last week.

headline: Flowers (hamstring) took part in individual drills at Friday's practice, Jeff Zrebiec of The Athletic reports.
story: This is the first sign of progress in Flowers' recovery from the hamstring injury that he suffered in the first half of the Ravens' Week 1 win at Indianapolis. Even if he goes down as a limited participant, though, he likely will be listed as questionable, at best, ahead of Sunday's game against the Cowboys in Rio de Janeiro.

headline: The Ravens listed Flowers (hamstring) as a non-participant in Thursday's practice.
story: As anticipated after he was spotted working out off to the side during the media-access portion of practice, Flowers went down as a non-participant for the second consecutive day. The wideout hasn't practiced in any fashion since tweaking his hamstring in the Ravens' season-opening win over the Colts, and he could be trending toward missing a second straight game this Sunday against the Cowboys in Rio de Janeiro. The Ravens were scheduled to fly to Brazil on Thursday, and, per Mike Garafolo of NFL Network, Flowers made the trip, so it seems as if he at least has a chance to play Week 3.

headline: Flowers (hamstring) isn't practicing Thursday, though he worked out off to the side prior to practice, Kyle Goon of The Baltimore Banner reports.
story: Flowers has yet to resume officially participating in practice since sustaining a hamstring injury during Baltimore's season-opening win over the Colts. The speedy wide receiver sat out the Week 2 loss to the Saints and is in danger of missing a second consecutive game Sunday against the Cowboys in Rio de Janeiro. Flowers would likely need to practice in at least some capacity Friday to have a chance to play Sunday.

headline: Flowers (hamstring) isn't participating in Wednesday's practice, Jamison Hensley of ESPN.com reports.
story: On Monday, head coach Jesse Minter said that Flowers had a "good shot" at playing in Sunday's game against the Cowboys in Brazil, after the star wideout missed the Ravens' Week 2 loss to the Saints due to the hamstring injury. However, with Flowers opening Week 3 prep as a spectator, his availability to return to action this Sunday now appears to be more uncertain. If Flowers ends up missing a second straight game, Rashod Bateman would be line for another turn as the Ravens' No. 1 receiver.

headline: Ravens head coach Jesse Minter said Monday that Flowers (hamstring) has a "good shot" to play Week 3 in Dallas, Ryan Mink of the Ravens' official site reports.
story: Listed as doubtful heading into this past Sunday's game against the Saints, Flowers was ultimately inactive for the Ravens' 24-17 loss. The team remains hopeful that Flowers' absence will be contained to just one game, and the wideout supported that optimism by returning to practice this past Friday as a limited participant. Baltimore will kick off its Week 3 prep Wednesday, and if Flowers upgrades to full practice participation that day, it would clear up any concern about his status heading into the matchup with the Cowboys.

headline: Flowers (hamstring) has been downgraded to out for Sunday's game against the Saints.
story: Typically, players listed as doubtful on final injury reports of the week are inactive on game days, but the Ravens got ahead of the issue and deemed Flowers unable to play one day prior. He thus will miss at least one contest as a result of the hamstring issue he suffered in Week 1, and Baltimore will roll with a receiving corps of Rashod Bateman, Devontez Walker, Elijah Sarratt and LaJohntay Wester in the meantime.

headline: Flowers (hamstring) is listed as doubtful for Sunday's game against New Orleans.
story: Flowers returned to practice Friday as a limited participant, with Jeff Zrebiec of The Athletic reporting that the wideout didn't do much during the open portion of practice. With Flowers unlikely to play, Baltimore's top wideouts for Week 2 are Rashod Bateman, Devontez Walker, Chris Moore, Elijah Sarratt and LaJohntay Wester.

headline: Flowers (hamstring) is practicing Friday, Jeff Zrebiec of The Athletic reports.
story: After missing Baltimore's first two practices of the week, Flowers is giving it a go at the final session. He'll likely be listed as a limited participant, with Zrebiec reporting that Flowers "didn't appear to be doing much" during the early portion of practice.

headline: Flowers (hamstring) was listed as a non-participant for Thursday's practice.
story: Flowers has missed the Ravens' first two practices ahead of Sunday's game versus the Saints. He caught five of six targets for 150 yards and a touchdown prior to exiting the Week 1 win over the Colts due to a hamstring injury, which has prevented Flowers from practicing in the lead-up to Week 2. Baltimore's top wide receiver will aim to practice Friday to give himself a chance to play come Sunday.

headline: Flowers (hamstring) was not spotted at Thursday's practice, Brian Wacker of The Baltimore Sun reports.
story: Flowers sat out Wednesday's session and did the same a day later. The speedy wide receiver will be hard-pressed to suit up Sunday if he's unable to practice in at least some capacity Friday. Fellow wide receiver Ja'Kobi Lane (wrist) was placed on injured reserve Wednesday, so Rashod Bateman, Devontez Walker, Elijah Sarratt and LaJohntay Wester are the only healthy options in Baltimore's wide receiver room at the moment.

headline: Flowers (hamstring) was listed as a non-participant for Wednesday's practice.
story: Flowers aggravated a hamstring issue from the preseason during Sunday's win over the Colts. He had piled up a career-high 150 yards in the first half but did not return to action after the aggravation. Coach Jesse Minter called Flowers day-to-day earlier Wednesday. Flowers' next chance to practice will come Thursday, but at this stage his status for Week 2 is murky at best. Baltimore's receiving depth is being tested early as rookie Ja'Kobi Lane (wrist) is on injured reserve after undergoing surgery.

headline: Coach Jesse Minter said Wednesday that Flowers (hamstring) still is considered day-to-day, Jamison Hensley of ESPN.com reports.
story: Prior to Minter's media session, Flowers wasn't spotted during the open portion of the Ravens' first Week 2 session. A hamstring injury stemming from the team's Week 1 win at Indianapolis is to blame, and Wednesday's practice report will reveal if Flowers was able to log any on-field reps.

headline: Flowers (hamstring) wasn't seen during the media-access portion of Wednesday's practice, Jeff Zrebiec of The Athletic reports.
story: Flowers ripped off five catches (on six targets) for 150 yards and one touchdown before departing late in the second quarter of this past Sunday's win at Indianapolis due to a hamstring issue. Coach Jesse Minter called Flowers "day-to-day" Monday, per Sam Cohn of The Baltimore Sun, with an expectation that the wide receiver won't miss much time. Wednesday's injury report will reveal if Flowers indeed went down as a non-participant or eventually was able to mix into drills.

headline: Henry rushed 24 times for 102 yards while catching one of two targets for an 18-yard touchdown in Sunday's 30-23 overtime win over the Falcons. He also ran in a two-point conversion.
story: Henry unsurprisingly worked as the focal point of Baltimore's offense in the absence of Lamar Jackson (ankle). The star running back pulled the Ravens within two points with his 18-yard touchdown catch in the third quarter. Baltimore's two-point conversion attempt after that touchdown failed, but Henry took matters into his own hands to convert a game-tying two-point conversion out of the wildcat formation with 40 seconds left in the fourth quarter. He then tacked on 32 rushing yards on Baltimore's touchdown drive in OT to top the century mark on the ground for the first time since Week 1. Henry has opened his 11th NFL season with a five-game touchdown streak, producing seven rushing touchdowns and one receiving score ahead of a Week 6 trip to Cleveland.

headline: Henry carried the ball 23 times for 73 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 24-18 win over the Titans. He also caught both his targets for six yards.
story: The star RB found the end zone for a fourth straight game to begin the season, rumbling in for a five-yard score on the Ravens' first possession. Henry already has seven rushing TDs, putting him firmly on pace for his ninth straight season in double digits, to go along with 374 rushing yards on 4.2 yards per carry. He'll look to extend his TD streak in in a Week 5 road trip to Atlanta.

headline: Henry rushed 26 times for 89 yards and two touchdowns while catching his lone target for no gain in Sunday's 34-31 win over the Cowboys.
story: Henry scored a four-yard rushing touchdown in the first quarter and a three-yard rushing touchdown in the second quarter, but he was denied the hat trick in the fourth quarter, when a would-be third rushing score was ruled down at the 1-yard line on replay, and Henry's subsequent effort to get in on fourth down was stuffed. The 32-year-old Henry is showing no signs of slowing down, as he has six touchdowns through three games and is averaging just over 100 rushing yards per game heading into a Week 4 home game against the winless Titans.

headline: Henry carried the ball 16 times for 68 yards and a touchdown and caught all three of his targets for 19 yards in Sunday's 24-17 loss to the Saints.
story: The five-time Pro Bowler punched it in from one yard out on a wildcat snap late in the first quarter to open the scoring. Henry wasn't able to break any big gains, however, with his longest run going for just eight yards. He's made four trips to the end zone in two games to begin the season, piling up 214 rushing yards and 38 receiving yards as well, and Henry will look to keep rolling in a Week 3 road trip to Dallas.

headline: Henry rushed 24 times for 144 yards and three touchdowns and brought in his only target for 19 yards in the Ravens' 41-23 win over the Colts on Sunday.
story: Much like he'd done at the expense of the Bills in Week 1 of last season, Henry turned in one of his signature performances right out of the gate, and he struck for his first two touchdowns in the first half from four and 32 yards away. The superstar running back added a three-yard scoring run early in the fourth quarter, and he consistently ripped off chunk gains throughout the afternoon at the expense of an overwhelmed Colts front. Henry's workload won't change under new head coach Jesse Minter if Sunday is any indication, and the perennial Pro Bowl back carries a stellar outlook for a Week 2 home matchup against a Saints defense that the Lions' Jahmyr Gibbs gashed for 156 rushing yards and two touchdowns Sunday.

headline: Henry will head into the Ravens' Week 1 game against the Colts with Justice Hill and Rasheen Ali as his backup options, Ryan Mink of the team's official site reports.
story: Though Keaton Mitchell is now with the Chargers after the Ravens non-tendered him back in the spring, Henry will be supported by a pair of familiar sidekicks. Ali is expected to serve as the Ravens' primary kickoff returner and will see most of his snaps on special teams, while Hill returns to his usual role as the top change-of-pace option. Rookie fifth-round pick Adam Randall (undisclosed) could also factor into the equation at some point this season, though not until at least Week 5 after the Ravens placed him on injured reserve. The makeup of the backfield once again points to the 32-year-old Henry handling a workhorse role in 2026, after he averaged 19.6 touches and exactly one touchdown per game over the prior two seasons.

headline: Washington (ankle) is questionable to return to Sunday night's contest against the Falcons.
story: Washington is dealing with an apparent ankle injury late in the second half, and his status for the final stretch of the contest is now unclear. In his absence, Nnamdi Madubuike and Calais Campbell will operare as the team's primary defensive ends.

headline: Stanley (toe) was able to complete Sunday's 24-18 win over Tennessee, Jonas Shaffer of TheBaltimoreBanner.com reports.
story: Stanley made his return to action Sunday after missing Week 3 while nursing a toe injury. After the victory, the left tackle noted he is still dealing with the issue, and that the injury was sustained in the first half of the team's Week 1 win against the Colts. Stanley seems likely to play Week 5 versus Atlanta, and he's hopeful the injury can heal on its own.

headline: Stanley (toe) is active against the Titans on Sunday.
story: Stanley was managing a toe injury during Week 4 prep, but the veteran offensive lineman has been officially cleared to play Sunday. He'll reclaim his starting spot at left tackle from Carson Vinson.

headline: Stanley (toe) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Titans.
story: Stanley opened Week 4 prep with back-to-back limited practices before sitting out of Friday's session for rest purposes. He's working through a toe injury that caused him to miss the Ravens' Week 3 win against the Cowboys, and his status for Sunday's game may not be known until about 90 minutes before the 1:00 p.m. ET kickoff, which is when the Ravens will announce their list of inactive players. Carson Vinson will likely start at left tackle for a second consecutive game if Stanley is not cleared to play against Tennessee.

headline: Stanley (toe) has been ruled out ahead of Sunday's game against the Cowboys.
story: Stanley did not log any practice participation during Week 3 prep. The starting left tackle aggravated a toe injury during the Ravens' Week 2 loss to the Saints, and it will now cost him one game at minimum while likely affording Carson Vinson a start against Dallas.

headline: Stanley (toe) did not participate in Wednesday's practice.
story: Stanley re-injured his toe in the Ravens' Week 2 loss to the Saints. The starting left tackle has been dealing with a toe issue since the team's Week 1 win over the Colts, and it remains to be seen if he'll ultimately be able to suit up for Sunday's Week 3 matchup against the Cowboys in Brazil.

headline: Stanley (toe) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Saints.
story: Stanley started Sunday's game after overcoming a persistent toe injury. The issue has flared up after some first-half snaps, and it is unclear if the left tackle will be able to return Sunday. Carson Vinson is the next man up at left tackle for the Ravens.

headline: Stanley (toe) is active for Sunday's game against the Saints.
story: Stanley earned himself the questionable tag for Week 2 after logging a DNP/DNP/LP practice log. He's dealing with a toe injury but has been cleared by medical staff to play Sunday, and he will assume his starting role at left tackle.

headline: Stanley (toe) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Saints.
story: Stanley missed the first two practices of the week due to a toe injury, but he was able to earn the questionable tag for Week 2 after practicing in a limited capacity Friday. Carson Vinson figures to be the top candidate to start at left tackle if Stanley is not cleared to play against New Orleans.

headline: Stanley (toe) did not participate in practice Thursday.
story: The starting left tackle also sat out of Wednesday's session. Stanley played for the entirety of the Ravens' Week 1 win over the Colts but emerged from the game with a toe injury. If he can't return to the field for this Sunday's matchup with the Saints, Carson Vinson will likely have to step in.

headline: Hamilton tallied 13 tackles (seven solo) during the Ravens' 24-17 loss to the Saints on Sunday.
story: Hamilton played all but one of the Ravens' 68 defensive snaps during Sunday's loss, and he was much more involved in the second half, with 10 of his career-high 13 tackles coming over the final two quarters. It was the eighth time in Hamilton's career that he logged 10-plus combined tackles, the most recent time having been Week 12 of the 2025 season. He's up to 18 combined tackles through two regular-season games and is well on pace to reach 100-plus tackles for a third consecutive year. Hamilton figures to be busy Week 3 against Dak Prescott, CeeDee Lamb and the Cowboys' passing attack.

headline: Hamilton logged five tackles (three solo) in Sunday's 41-23 win over the Colts.
story: Hamilton played all 54 of the Ravens' defensive snaps in the contest, holding the Colts to 23 points on 12 possessions. The star defensive back has stepped into a bigger role at slot cornerback in 2026 due to the presence of Jaylinn Hawkins and Malaki Starks at safety.

headline: Johnson (hamstring) was considered limited at the Bills' walkthrough practice Wednesday.
story: Johnson reeled in all four of his targets for 72 yards during Monday night's 37-34 overtime win against the Rams, but he may have picked up a hamstring injury in the process. The running back's ability to be limited Wednesday is a positive sign, but he'll have two more chances to log a full practice and erase any concern about his availability for Sunday's contest versus Las Vegas.

headline: Johnson caught all four of his targets for 72 yards during the Bills' 37-34 overtime win over the Rams on Monday.
story: Johnson played only 14 of the Bills' 64 offensive snaps (21.9 percent) and didn't log a single carry. However, the veteran running back made his snaps count as a receiver, rumbling for 40 yards on his first catch midway through the second quarter to set up a 17-yard touchdown run by James Cook on the very next play. Johnson added three more catches, including a 26-yard grab, and finished second on the Bills in receiving yards behind Khalil Shakir's 80. Johnson will continue to operate as the Bills' change-of-pace back heading into Week 7 against the Raiders.

headline: Johnson rushed once for three yards and caught both of his targets for nine yards Sunday in a loss to New England.
story: Johnson logged 19 offensive snaps, well ahead of the four snaps played by Ray Davis and well behind the 35 snaps logged by starter James Cook. Johnson logged 50 receiving yards in his season debut in Week 3, and six of his seven touches this season have been receptions, so he clearly has a role as a pass catcher in Buffalo's offense. With that said, Johnson doesn't have a reliable weekly fantasy floor and isn't a trustworthy fantasy asset as long as Cook is healthy.

headline: Johnson (hamstring) does not have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Chargers, Alec White of the Bills' official site reports. "Ty Johnson will be good to go," coach Joe Brady said Friday.
story: He missed both of the first two games of the season, but with receivers DJ Moore (shoulder) and Keon Coleman (ankle) both being listed as questionable, Johnson's receiving skills out of the backfield might be useful for the offense. Johnson really isn't recommended for fantasy unless anything happens to starter James Cook, but the former's presence on the field does knock Ray Davis down a peg.

headline: Johnson (hamstring) practiced fully Wednesday.
story: Johnson thus is poised for his season debut Sunday against the Chargers after missing the first two games of the campaign due to a hamstring issue. Working behind James Cook and vying with Ray Davis for complementary RB reps doesn't afford Johnson much in terms of touches, as he's earned 170 in 44 regular-season games over the last three years as a member of the Bills.

headline: Johnson (hamstring) is listed as inactive Thursday against the Lions.
story: Despite being listed as limited on all three of the Bills' Week 2 injury reports, Johnson will continue to don street clothes on game days due to a hamstring issue that has bothered him since at least Aug. 24. In Johnson's absence, Ray Davis will continue to garner RB reps that don't go to starter James Cook, while Frank Gore is on hand in case one of those two leaves the game for any reason.

headline: Johnson (hamstring) is listed as questionable for Thursday's game against the Lions.
story: Johnson sat out the Week 1 victory over the Texans. He returned to a limited practice Tuesday, but he's not quite in the clear yet, and his status will probably come down to the wire for the primetime game Thursday. No Buffalo running back has much value outside of insurance behind bell-cow back James Cook, and now Frank Gore has had a chance to enter the mix as yet another option in the Buffalo backfield.

headline: Johnson (hamstring) was a limited participant in Tuesday's practice.
story: Johnson has opened Week 2 prep with back-to-back limited practices, and Wednesday's report will provide clarity on whether he'll be available for Thursday night's home tilt against the Lions. The veteran running back is currently working through a right hamstring injury, and he's been dealing with lower-body issues since early training camp. Frank Gore would likely be elevated from the practice squad and serve as Buffalo's RB3 behind James Cook and Ray Davis if Johnson is not cleared to play against Detroit.

headline: The Bills listed Johnson (hamstring) as a limited participant on Monday's estimated practice report.
story: After missing the Bills' first two practices of Week 1, Johnson returned to the field Friday as a limited participant and took a questionable tag into Sunday's season opener versus the Texans. Johnson ultimately was inactive for the 36-31 win, but he'll have a stronger chance of making his 2026 debut Thursday against the Lions if he can upgrade to full participation in practice at some point over the next two days.

headline: Johnson (hamstring) is inactive Week 1 against the Texans.
story: Johnson was able to log only a single limited practice this week, and the 28-year-old back entered Sunday with a "questionable" tag. He'll ultimately sit against Houston, leaving a few more backfield snaps to starter James Cook and backup Ray Davis. Johnson and the Bills have a short week ahead, as they're set to take on the Lions in a Week 2 matchup Thursday night. If Johnson does end up suiting up then, he'll likely return to his role as a passing down specialist and special-teamer, similar to his last few seasons in Buffalo.

headline: Johnson (hamstring) is questionable for Sunday's game at Houston, Joe Buscaglia of The Athletic reports.
story: Johnson just returned to practice Thursday after missing a month, but head coach Joe Brady said Friday that the veteran running back "doesn't need a lot of the physical work to go do his job." If Johnson ends up inactive, it could push more snaps and targets toward starter James Cook, in addition to benefitting backup Ray Davis. The Bills have typically deployed Johnson as a passing-down specialist.

headline: Johnson (hamstring) is practicing Friday, but Alex Brasky of SI.com believes the running back is unlikely to play Sunday in Houston.
story: Johnson returned to practice Thursday after missing a full month, so the Bills will probably wait until Week 2 or 3 to have him suit up. James Cook could get a few extra snaps in passing situations, while Ray Davis also gets a minor boost for workload projection in Johnson's absence.

headline: Johnson (hamstring) didn't practice Thursday, Matt Parrino of The Syracuse Post-Standard reports.
story: Johnson continues to miss practice due to the hamstring injury, which has kept him sidelined since Aug. 8. Though Johnson avoided placement on injured reserve coming out of the preseason, his 2026 debut could be delayed until at least Week 2 if he's unable to practice in some capacity Friday. In the event Johnson is sidelined for Sunday's season opener versus the Texans, Frank Gore could be elevated from the practice squad to provide a third option in the backfield behind James Cook and Ray Davis.

headline: Johnson (lower leg) isn't participating in Wednesday's practice, Joe Buscaglia of The Athletic reports.
story: Johnson has been a spectator for practices since Aug. 8, when he appeared to sustain a right leg injury during a 1-on-1 drill. Though he still has two more days to potentially fit in some on-field work prior to Sunday's game against the Texans, Johnson may be trending toward an absence in Week 1. If Johnson ends up missing the season opener, the Bills would have more snaps on passing downs available for lead back James Cook.

headline: Johnson (lower leg) remains sidelined at Tuesday's practice, Joe Buscaglia of The Athletic reports.
story: Johnson exited practice in early August and has been dealing with some sort of issue in his leg for the better part of a full month now. He resumed running and sprinting last week. Turning 29 later this month, Johnson has carved out a role on game days with the Bills, but he's more of a nuisance than anything in fantasy. Even if James Cook were to go down with an injury, Johnson's role likely wouldn't change all that much, as Ray Davis is Cook's more direct backup as a rusher. Johnson has averaged just 3.9 touches per game over his 34 regular-season appearances dating back to the start of the 2024 campaign.

headline: Johnson (lower leg) didn't practice Tuesday, but head coach Joe Brady said that the running back has resumed sprinting, Jay Skurski of The Buffalo News reports.
story: Though Johnson hasn't practiced in more than two weeks while nursing a lower-leg injury and looks unlikely to play in Thursday's preseason finale versus the Steelers, Brady noted that the running back is "in a good head space" and could still be available for Week 1 in Houston. If Johnson ends up being sidelined to begin the regular season, however, lead back James Cook could take on a heightened role on passing downs.

headline: Johnson (lower leg) didn't practice Monday, Ryan Miller of the Rochester Democrat and Chronicle reports.
story: Per the report, Johnson, who hasn't practiced since Aug. 8, was on the field before Saturday's preseason game against the Browns wearing a sleeve on his right leg. At this stage, he doesn't seem likely to suit up for the Bills' exhibition finale, but when he is able able to return to the field, Johnson will have a chance to re-enter the equation in a Buffalo backfield led by James Cook that also includes Ray Davis.

headline: Palmer (shoulder) was listed as a limited participant at the Bills' walkthrough practice Wednesday.
story: Palmer suffered a shoulder injury at practice and was ultimately unavailable for the team's Week 5 win over the Rams on Monday Night Football. Although the team didn't officially practice, the wide receiver's limited participation is a positive sign. Palmer will have two more chances to officially practice in full prior to Sunday's matchup with the Raiders.

headline: Palmer (shoulder) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Rams, Katherine Fitzgerald of The Buffalo News reports.
story: Palmer popped up on Friday's injury report as a limited participant due to a shoulder issue, which appears to be severe enough for him to miss his first game of the season. With DJ Moore (shoulder) listed as questionable, the Bills' top pass catching options could be Khalil Shakir, Keon Coleman and Dalton Kincaid, and rookie Skyler Bell is expected to make his NFL debut after being a healthy scratch in each of the first four games of the regular season, per Joe Buscaglia of The Athletic. Palmer's next chance to play is Week 6 against the Raiders on Sunday, Oct. 18.

headline: Palmer caught one of three targets for a 43-yard touchdown in Thursday's 41-31 win over the Lions.
story: Palmer didn't score at all last season in his first campaign with the Bills, but he's now found the end zone in back-to-back weeks. He's hauled in just one pass in each of the first two games, but he could see more looks if DJ Moore's shoulder injury puts him on the shelf for a stint. Palmer, Khalil Shakir and Keon Coleman would likely work as the main wide-receiver trio if Moore can't suit up in Week 3 against the Chargers.

headline: Palmer caught one of his two targets for a 34-yard touchdown in Sunday's 36-31 win over the Texans.
story: Palmer's only targets in Week 1 came on the last two offensive plays of the game for the Bills. Josh Allen missed the wide receiver on a deep ball he couldn't quite react to before delivering a laser between Kamari Lassiter and Calen Bullock to Palmer for what ended up being the game-winning touchdown. Palmer's 18 offensive snaps prove the wide receiver has some week-to-week upside despite not being a primary option in Buffalo's offense.

headline: The Bills list all of DJ Moore, Khalil Shakir and Keon Coleman (foot) ahead of Palmer on their unofficial depth chart for Week 1 posted Tuesday, Lance Lysowski of The Buffalo News reports.
story: During his first season in Buffalo in 2025, Palmer produced a 22-303-0 receiving line on 37 targets over his 12 appearances before missing both of the team's playoff contests due to an ankle injury. Though he was declared fully healthy ahead of training camp, Palmer looks like he may have been surpassed in the pecking order at receiver by Coleman, a 2024 second-round pick who showed promise as a rookie but fell out of favor with the Bills toward the end of the past season. While the Bills retained most of their offensive coaching staff from 2025 with Joe Brady getting promoted from coordinator to head coach after Sean McDermott was dismissed, Coleman appears to be entering the upcoming season with a clean slate and could be prioritized ahead of Palmer, whose need as a vertical threat had already been lessened following the acquisition of Moore.

headline: Moore (shoulder) was listed as a non-participant on Wednesday's estimated injury report.
story: The Bills conducted a walkthrough Wednesday after playing Monday night, but Moore would not have gotten any work in had the Bills decided to practice. Moore will have a couple chances to practice before the week comes to a close, but with Buffalo on bye in Week 7, the team could decide to hold him out again Sunday in an effort to maximize the recovery time.

headline: Moore (shoulder) is listed as inactive Monday at the Rams.
story: After suffering a shoulder injury in Week 4, Moore wasn't expected to be tending to a long-term issue, and head coach Joe Brady told Katherine Fitzgerald of The Buffalo News on Thursday that the wide receiver was "going to be able to do everything he can to be able to rock this week." Moore then managed just one limited session (Saturday) during Week 5 prep, which wasn't enough for him to gain clearance to play Monday. With both Moore and Joshua Palmer (shoulder) unavailable, Khalil Shakir, Keon Coleman, Greg Dortch, Skyler Bell and Trent Sherfield will handle WR reps for the Bills.

headline: Moore (shoulder) is listed as questionable for Monday's game against the Rams, Katherine Fitzgerald of The Buffalo News reports.
story: Moore was able to participate in Saturday's practice in a limited capacity after being sidelined for the first two sessions of Week 5 prep, and that's enough for the veteran wide receiver to draw the questionable tag for Monday night's contest. Joshua Palmer (shoulder) has already been ruled out, so if Moore is also sidelined, then Khalil Shakir and Keon Coleman would operate as the top wide receivers for Buffalo.

headline: Moore (shoulder) was on the field for the start of Saturday's practice, Joe Buscaglia of The Athletic reports.
story: Moore was a non-participant in each of the Bills' first two practices of the week, so it's a positive sign for him to be on the field for Saturday's session. The Bills' injury report following practice will provide clarity on Moore's status for Monday night's road game against the Rams, and if the veteran wide receiver cannot play, then Khalil Shakir and Keon Coleman would serve as Buffalo's top wide receivers, with tight end Dalton Kincaid also in the mix for more targets from quarterback Josh Allen.

headline: Moore (shoulder) remained a non-participant in Friday's practice for the Bills.
story: With back-to-back absences, Moore isn't looking great for Monday's game at the Rams, though he'll still have one more chance Saturday to practice. If Moore doesn't end up playing, Keon Coleman and Joshua Palmer (shoulder) will be the top candidates to replace Moore's snaps, with slot receiver Khalil Shakir and tight end Dalton Kincaid potentially helping to pick up the slack in terms of target volume.

headline: Moore (shoulder) was not on the field for the start of Friday's practice open to the media, Joe Buscaglia of The Athletic reports.
story: Moore has logged back-to-back DNPs to start Week 5 prep, but he does have an extra day to get ready, with the Bills and Rams not kicking off until Monday night. However, fantasy managers are going to need to have a backup plan in place if Moore doesn't get the green light to play after he aggravated his shoulder injury in last Sunday's loss to the Patriots. Dalton Kincaid, Khalil Shakir, Keon Coleman and Joshua Palmer would all be in line for elevated roles in the passing game if Moore ends up inactive.

headline: Moore (shoulder) didn't practice Thursday.
story: Moore made an early departure this past Sunday against the Patriots in the second quarter with a shoulder injury and wasn't able to return. While the issue isn't considered to be long term and head coach Joe Brady didn't rule Moore out for Monday's game at the Rams as of Thursday, per Katherine Fitzgerald of The Buffalo News, the wide receiver kicked off the week with no on-field work. Moore will have two more chances to prove his health before the Bills potentially make a ruling on his status once they post Saturday's injury report.

headline: Moore (shoulder) was not participating during the media viewing period of Thursday's practice,  Sal Capaccio of WGR Sports Radio 550 Buffalo reports.
story: Moore has not been ruled out for the Week 5 matchup against the Rams, but it seems he's got an uphill battle ahead of him. He aggravated his shoulder injury in the Week 4 loss to the Patriots and did not return to action. He may get some work in later in Thursday's session, but the official injury report will tell the tale.

headline: Head coach Joe Brady said Thursday that Moore (shoulder) is "going to be able to do everything he can to be able to rock this week," Katherine Fitzgerald of The Buffalo News reports.
story: Moore aggravated a shoulder injury during Buffalo's Week 4 loss to the Patriots. Brady didn't have a specific update on Moore's status Thursday, but it sounds like the veteran wide receiver at least has a chance to avoid missing Monday's game against the Rams. Moore has a 92-game regular-season ironman streak on the line.

headline: Moore (shoulder) is dealing with an injury that isn't considered long-term, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
story: Moore exited Sunday's loss to the Patriots after aggravating a previous shoulder injury. He isn't expected to miss significant time, though it remains to be seen if Moore will play against the Rams in Week 5. The 29-year-old wide receiver has suited up for 92 consecutive regular-season games dating back to the 2020 season.

headline: Moore (shoulder) is considered doubtful to return to Sunday's contest versus the Patriots.
story: Moore went to the sideline in the second quarter and was diagnosed with a shoulder injury, which may be an aggravation of the issue he's tended to since Week 2. If Moore is unable to reenter Sunday's game, Khalil Shakir, Keon Coleman, Joshua Palmer and even Greg Dortch will be on hand for WR reps in the Bills offense.

headline: Moore departed Sunday's contest against the Patriots due to a shoulder injury.
story: Moore was shaken up on a play in the second quarter and immediately went to the sideline tent. This may stem from the shoulder issue he sustained in Week 2, but he nonetheless is considered questionable to return for the time being.

headline: Moore (shoulder) was limited in Friday's practice but doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against New England.
story: Moore is still managing the shoulder injury he sustained in Week 2 against the Lions. While he was limited in practice all week, the veteran wideout should play his normal allotment of snaps against the Patriots after pacing the team in routes and targets last Sunday against the Chargers.

headline: Moore (shoulder) is practicing in a non-contact jersey Friday, Sal Capaccio of WGR Sports Radio 550 Buffalo reports.
story: Moore has been limited in practice all week, as he continues to deal with the shoulder injury he suffered in Week 2 against the Lions. The veteran wideout played through the issue last Sunday against the Chargers and ran a team-high 23 routes while seeing 10 targets from Josh Allen. Assuming Moore didn't suffer a setback, he should be able to play Sunday against New England.

headline: Moore (shoulder) remained a limited participant at Thursday's practice.
story: Moore didn't practice much leading up to Buffalo's Week 3 win over the Chargers, but he proceeded to suit up and caught six of 10 targets for 67 yards in the victory. Per Sal Capaccio of WGR Sports Radio 550 Buffalo, the veteran wide receiver once again sported a no-contact jersey during Thursday's practice, but he still looks on track to play Sunday against the Patriots. If Moore can upgrade to full participation Friday, he'll likely avoid taking a questionable tag into the weekend.

headline: Moore (shoulder) was limited in Wednesday's practice.
story: Moore was limited last week in practice after he was injured in Buffalo's Week 2 game against the Lions. The veteran wideout still played through it last Sunday against the Chargers and played 42 of 66 offensive snaps while running a team-high 23 routes on Josh Allen's 31 dropbacks. Moore turned 10 targets into six catches for 67 yards. He should be fine for Week 4 against New England.

headline: Moore brought in six of 10 targets for 67 yards in the Bills' 24-16 win over the Chargers on Sunday.
story: Making his return from an early Week 2 exit due to a shoulder injury, Moore jumped right back into the swing of things by leading the Bills in receptions, receiving yards and targets. The veteran wideout has made an impact in both of his non-injury-shortened games with Josh Allen, producing an 11-167-1 line on 18 targets. Moore figures to continue commanding the majority of Allen's attention in a Week 4 home matchup against the Patriots next Sunday.

headline: Moore (shoulder) is listed as active for Sunday's game against the Chargers.
story: It was reported shortly before kickoff that Moore was expected to suit up Sunday, and he will indeed do so. It's unclear how close Moore is to 100 percent after sandwiching a couple limited practices around a Thursday 'DNP' on the injury report, so it remains to be seen if he will fill his usual role in Week 3.

headline: Moore (shoulder) is in line to suit up for Sunday's game against the Chargers, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
story: When Moore was listed as questionable for Week 3 action Friday, head coach Joe Brady told Katherine Fitzgerald of The Buffalo News that the wide receiver would be a game-time decision. Moore had sandwiched limited sessions around an absence Thursday prior to those comments due to an AC joint sprain that he suffered in Week 2 against the Lions, but Schefter's report Sunday morning indicates that he'll avoid the Bills' inactive list about 90 minutes before a 1:00 p.m. ET kickoff.

headline: Head coach Joe Brady said Friday that Moore (shoulder) will be listed as questionable and a game-time decision for Sunday's contest against the Chargers, Katherine Fitzgerald of The Buffalo News reports.
story: Moore made an early exit from the Bills' Week 2 win against the Lions due to an AC joint sprain, and while he was able to practice in a limited capacity Wednesday, he sat out Thursday's session before returning to drills Friday in a red non-contact jersey. Both Moore and fellow WR Keon Coleman (ankle) are considered game-time calls for Week 3 action, but both players' statuses will be confirmed by about 90 minutes before Sunday's 1:00 p.m. ET kickoff.

headline: Moore (shoulder) was back on the practice field Friday in a red non-contact jersey, Katherine Fitzgerald of The Buffalo News reports.
story: After a limited practice to start the week, Moore was held out Thursday. He's now back practicing with his teammates, though it sounds like he'll be listed as a limited participant and may get an injury designation for Sunday's matchup with the Chargers.

headline: Moore (shoulder) was listed as a non-participant in Thursday's practice.
story: Moore kicked off Week 3 prep Wednesday as a limited participant, but it's unclear if his lack of activity a day later was the result of a setback or more of a pre-planned maintenance day while he tends to an AC joint sprain in his shoulder. In any case, what Moore is able to do during the Bills' final practice of the week Friday will ultimately determine whether he takes a designation into Sunday's game against the Chargers.

headline: Moore (shoulder) was not spotted on the practice field at the beginning of Thursday's session, Joe Buscaglia of The Athletic reports.
story: There's still a chance Moore joins his teammates for practice Thursday ,but it's noteworthy nonetheless that he's not there as things get underway. Moore, who suffered an AC joint sprain in the Week 2 win over the Lions, reportedly "felt great" after Wednesday's practice, though he was in a non-contact jersey. The rest of the week will give more clarity on Moore's status as Sunday approaches. Buscaglia added that Keon Coleman (ankle) also was absent for the start of Thursday's session.

headline: Moore (shoulder) "felt great" after getting in a limited practice Wednesday, Matt Parrino of The Syracuse Post-Standard reports.
story: Moore did not take contact Wednesday and officially did not get in a full session, but he was optimistic about his status when asked about it afterward. While Moore is taking the positive path and there is reason to believe he will suit up Sunday against the Chargers, it remains to be seen if he will do so.

headline: Moore (shoulder) was spotted participating in Wednesday's practice while wearing a red non-contact jersey, Katherine Fitzgerald of The Buffalo News reports.
story: Moore made an early exit from the Bills' Week 2 win over the Lions due to an AC joint sprain, logging just 23 snaps while finishing with no targets and one carry for minus-1 yard during his limited time on the field. Though he appears set to go down as a limited practice participant on the Bills' first Week 3 injury report, Moore's presence on the field is generally a positive sign for his chances of suiting up Sunday versus the Chargers.

headline: The Bills are treating Moore as day-to-day after he was diagnosed with an AC joint sprain in his shoulder after exiting Thursday's 41-31 win over the Lions, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
story: Moore carried once for minus-1 yard and didn't draw a target on his 23 snaps before exiting Thursday's contest late in the second quarter. Keon Coleman (55 snaps, 6-63-0 line on six targets) saw a boosted profile on offense in Moore's absence, but Coleman could fade into more of a tertiary role in the passing game if Moore is able to play through the shoulder injury during the Bills' Week 3 matchup with the Chargers. Rapoport relays that Moore is expected to practice next week, and the Bills will see how his shoulder responds before his status for next Sunday's contest is clarified.

headline: Moore (shoulder) is believed to have sustained an AC joint sprain in Thursday's victory over the Lions, and although "it's not a serious injury" he is uncertain for Week 3., Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
story: Head coach Joe Brady did not provide a postgame update on Moore after he left Thursday's contest in the second quarter, but more details are now available, and it appears Moore is not facing any sort of extended absence. He will have over a week to rest and recover before the Bills square off against the Chargers, and if he's unable to go by then that will mean more snaps for Khalil Shakir, Keon Coleman and Joshua Palmer.

headline: Moore (shoulder) has been ruled out for the remainder of Thursday night's game against the Lions.
story: Moore exited late in the second quarter and was taken to the locker room for X-rays. The results of those tests aren't yet clear, but Moore appeared to be in a considerable amount of pain after landing hard on his shoulder while attempting a diving catch in the end zone. Prior to his departure, Moore rushed one time for minus-1 yard and didn't see an official target in the passing game. Khalil Shakir and Dalton Kincaid figure to be Josh Allen's preferred targets the rest of the way, with Keon Coleman, Joshua Palmer and Dawson Knox filling in behind them in the pecking order.

headline: Moore (shoulder) is questionable to return to Thursday night's game against the Lions.
story: The Bills also are concerned about a possible stinger for Moore after he was injured late in the second quarter while diving for a pass in the end zone. Moore looked to be in considerable pain and is undergoing X-rays. Khalil Shakir, Keon Coleman and Joshua Palmer figure to see the bulk of the wide receiver snaps while Moore is in the locker room.

headline: Moore exited Thursday night's game against the Lions in the second quarter with a shoulder injury, Sal Capaccio of WGR Sports Radio 550 Buffalo reports.
story: Moore was injured while attempting a diving catch in the end zone late in the second quarter. He immediately grabbed at his shoulder or collarbone area and was assisted off the field with trainers before being taken to the locker room. Prior to leaving, Moore failed to record any receptions. Khalil Shakir, Keon Coleman and Joshua Palmer will have to pick up the slack at wide receiver with Moore sidelined.

headline: Moore caught five of eight targets for 100 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 36-31 win over the Texans.
story: Moore made a strong first impression with the Bills, highlighted by a 43-yard touchdown catch in the second quarter. The 29-year-old wide receiver had a career-low 682 receiving yards in 17 regular-season games with the Bears last year, but he has exceeded 1,000 yards in four of eight regular seasons split between the Panthers and Bears. Josh Allen spread the ball around as usual against Houston, but Moore paced the team with eight targets. Moore will look to build on this productive debut in Thursday's home opener against the Lions.

headline: Moore didn't play against the Steelers in Thursday's exhibition victory.
story: Buffalo elected to rest the bulk of its projected regular-season starters, including Moore, for the team's final preseason game. The veteran wideout saw action in one exhibition contest, catching three of four targets for 61 yards. Moore left that game early due to an ankle injury but has since returned to practice, so he should be good to go as the Bills' top wideout Week 1 of the regular season versus a tough Texans defense.

headline: Moore (lower body) is participating in team drills Thursday, Matthew Bove of 7 News WKBW reports.
story: Moore was limited in practice Tuesday after getting banged up in preseason action Saturday against the Panthers. He has progressed back to full participation Thursday, indicating that the injury is no longer hampering him. Buffalo is battling injuries to its wide receiver room behind Moore, as Khalil Shakir (undisclosed), Keon Coleman (foot) and Skyler Bell (lower body) are all hurt.

headline: Jackson (knee) is inactive against the Rams on Monday.
story: Jackson was initially listed as questionable due to a knee injury, which is severe enough for the second-year pro to miss his first game of the regular season. Greg Gaines and DeWayne Carter are in line for more rotational reps on the Bills' defensive line due to Jackson's absence.

headline: Jackson (knee) is listed as questionable for Monday's game against the Rams, Joe Buscaglia of The Athletic reports.
story: Jackson's practice reps were limited due to a knee injury, and his status for Monday's game may not be officially known until the Bills announce their list of inactive players approximately 90 minutes before the 8:15 p.m. ET kickoff. Ed Oliver (knee) has already been ruled out, so DeWayne Carter and Greg Gaines would both be in line for even more defensive snaps if Jackson is not cleared to play.

headline: Sanders (appendix) practiced in full Thursday.
story: Sanders missed Week 1 due to a knee injury and then had an appendectomy. He logged two limited practices last week but didn't play versus New England on Sunday. However, with a full practice under his belt to begin Week 5 prep, Sanders is a good bet to suit up Monday night against the Rams.

headline: Sanders (appendix) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Patriots.
story: Sanders is still healing from appendix surgery on Sep. 22, though he did return to practice Thursday. Landon Jackson may get more playing time alongside Ed Oliver and Deone Walker while Sanders is out.

headline: Sanders (appendix) was a limited practice participant Thursday.
story: Sanders underwent surgery to have his appendix removed on Tuesday, Sept. 22, and he didn't play in Week 3 against the Chargers. The second-year pro didn't practice Wednesday to begin Week 4 prep, but he was able to participate in a limited capacity Thursday. That's a good sign Sanders is healing well, though it remains to be seen if he'll be ready to suit up Sunday versus New England.

headline: Sanders (appendix) won't play in Sunday's game against the Chargers.
story: Sanders underwent an appendectomy Tuesday, so it's unknown how long he will be off the field. With Ed Oliver (hip) questionable, Landon Jackson may be busier than usual.

headline: Sanders (appendix) did not participate in Wednesday's practice, Katherine Fitzgerald of The Buffalo News reports.
story: Sanders did not play in the Bills' Week 2 win over the Lions due to a knee injury and an illness. The defensive tackle's absence during the first practice of Week 3 came for a different reason, as Sanders' appendix was surgically removed Tuesday. It remains unclear how long it will take the 23-year-old to return to football shape.

headline: Sanders (knee/illness) is officially listed as inactive for Thursday's game versus the Lions.
story: Sanders was sidelined by a knee injury in Week 1 and then came down with an illness earlier in the week, and the combination of both leaves him unavailable for Week 2. In his absence, 2024 third-rounder DeWayne Carter figures to continue to see increased work on the defensive line.

headline: Sanders (knee/illness) is questionable for Buffalo's game against Detroit on Thursday.
story: Sanders is still battling the illness and knee injury that forced him to miss the team's Week 1 win over the Texans. If he ends up being good to go on Thursday, the 23-year-old will be in line to serve as one of the Bills' starting defensive linemen for the matchup versus the Lions.

headline: Sanders (knee/illness) did not participate in Tuesday's practice.
story: Sanders has come down with an illness and is not ready to suit up as he battles both his immune system and a lingering knee issue. The defensive tackle was inactive for Buffalo's Week 1 game against Houston and is trending toward missing Thursday night's game against Detroit as well.

headline: Sanders (knee) is inactive for Week 1 against the Texans.
story: Sanders missed practice Thursday, sandwiched by a pair of limited sessions both Wednesday and Friday. It ultimately wasn't enough for the second-year player and potential starter to get clearance, leaving the likes of Landon Jackson and DeWayne Carter in line for more rotational snaps.

headline: Sanders (knee) did not participate at practice Thursday.
story: Sanders recorded a limited practice Wednesday, but it seems he may have suffered some sort of setback during the week. He'll likely need to return to practice Friday to give himself a chance to be active in Week 1 at Houston.

headline: Davis caught his lone target for 31 yards while adding two carries for two yards and three kickoff returns for 114 yards during the Bills' 37-34 overtime win over the Rams on Monday.
story: Davis opened Monday's contest in style with a 70-yard return on the opening kickoff that set the Bills up deep in Rams territory, though the Rams defense forced a three-and-out and Buffalo had to settle for a 49-yard field goal. Davis made another big contribution early in the fourth quarter, when he turned a screen pass into a 31-yard gain before being tackled just short of the goal line, which led to a one-yard touchdown run by Josh Allen on the next play. Davis has been limited mostly to work on special teams while mixing in occasionally in the back field. That said, Davis and Ty Johnson could both be in the mix for more offensive touches, given that head coach Joe Brady said Tuesday that "...at some point there has to be consequences" in reference to James Cook's fumble issues this season, per Nick Suss of ESPN.com. The Bills will stay on the road for Week 6 against the Raiders on Oct. 18.

headline: Davis logged a four-yard carry, a three-yard reception and returned one kickoff for 29 yards during the Bills' 29-26 loss to the Patriots in Week 4.
story: Both of Davis' offensive outputs came on back-to-back plays early in the second quarter, and his four snaps on offense were well behind starter James Cook (35) and backup Ty Johnson (19). Even as a returner, Davis took a back seat to Greg Dortch, the latter of whom returned four kickoffs for 91 yards and two punts for 16 yards. Davis' production on offense and special teams will continue to be limited unless one of Cook, Johnson or Dortch were to miss time.

headline: Davis (hamstring) is expected to play against the Patriots on Sunday.
story: Davis was questionable heading into Sunday's game after participating as a limited participant in Friday's practice. The 26-year-old has one rushing attempt through three regular-season games for three yards.

headline: Davis (hamstring) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Patriots.
story: Davis popped up on the injury report Thursday as a full participant, which would suggest he was possibly injured at the end of that practice. If Davis is unable to play in Week 4, Ty Johnson and Frank Gore will likely handle the backup duties behind James Cook.

headline: Davis played five snaps on offense and five snaps on special teams without showing up in the box score otherwise in the Bills' 24-16 win over the Chargers on Sunday.
story: Davis' catch for no gain early in the fourth quarter was negated by a holding penalty by Alec Anderson. It appears Davis will not be a factor in the Bills' offensive game plan this season, with Ty Johnson serving as the backup option in the backfield for James Cook. Davis should continue to see the field as a contributor on special teams, though he did not return a kickoff after doing so in both of the first two games of the regular season.

headline: Davis returned one kickoff for 31 yards during Thursday's 41-31 win versus the Lions.
story: Davis logged just eight offensive snaps in Week 2 despite Ty Johnson (hamstring) being inactive, and he did not record any carries or receptions. It appears unlikely he'll have much fantasy utility in the near future unless starter James Cook misses time.

headline: Davis rushed one time for three yards in Buffalo's 36-31 win over the Texans on Sunday.
story: Frank Gore actually out-snapped Davis 10 to five behind James Cook, as both Davis and Gore rushed one time for three yards. If something were to ever happen to Cook, it looks like Gore could actually have a bigger role than expected, making Davis a shakier bench stash in fantasy.

headline: Davis didn't receive a touch on offense but gained 11 yards on two punt returns while losing a fumble in Thursday's 28-27 preseason win over the Steelers.
story: His muffed punt return at the Buffalo 12-yard line in the first quarter led directly to Pittsburgh's first TD of the game on the very next play. It was a tough way for Davis to end his preseason, but the third-year RB has never returned a punt in his NFL career. Davis' spot as the No. 2 back behind James Cook seems fairly secure however, after he averaged 4.7 yards on 58 carries over 17 regular-season games last year.

headline: Davis rushed seven times for 21 yards and a touchdown while adding a 10-yard catch on his lone target in Saturday's 31-7 preseason win over the Browns.
story: Davis got the start at running back due to James Cook resting. Davis, a 2024 fourth-round pick, capped Buffalo's opening drive with a one-yard touchdown run and stayed in for the team's second possession. Cook will continue to lead Buffalo's backfield in the regular season as long as he's healthy, but Davis would be a must-roster fantasy option running behind Buffalo's elite offensive line if Cook gets hurt.

headline: Davis carried the ball three times for 21 yards and caught all four of his targets for 32 yards in Saturday's 29-14 preseason win over the Panthers.
story: James Cook got the start in the backfield during the Bills' preseason opener and played the whole first quarter, but Davis was the next RB into the game and had a very productive day. Davis' numbers as a pass-catcher were surprising considering that the third-year back has just 27 career catches in 34 regular-season contests, but new offensive coordinator Pete Carmichael has suggested that Cook could see more usage as a receiver in 2026, and Davis might benefit from that wrinkle in the scheme as well when he's on the field.

headline: Danna re-signed with the Bills on Tuesday.
story: Danna was released by Buffalo on Monday but he will return to the team after one day as a free agent. The 28-year-old has appeared in one contest with the team this season, failing to record any stats while logging eight defensive snaps and a one snap with the special-teams unit in Week 2 versus Detroit.

headline: Buffalo released Danna on Monday.
story: In a corresponding transaction, the Bills signed cornerback Anthony Kendall from their practice squad to their 53-man roster Monday. Danna will become an unrestricted free agent and likely start to seek another opportunity with a different team.

headline: Coleman caught a seven-yard touchdown pass on two targets during the Bills' 37-34 overtime win over the Rams on Monday.
story: It was a statistically quiet night for Coleman despite the fact that DJ Moore (shoulder) was inactive, but Josh Allen completed only 12 of 19 passes and the Bills got most of their yardage on the ground. Coleman did have catches of 17 and seven yards in the third quarter negated by penalties, but the third-year pro was wide open for his touchdown after two Rams defensive backs collided. Coleman's 45 offensive snaps led all Bills wide receivers, and he has a 15-224-2 receiving line on 18 targets through five regular-season games. The Bills will stay on the road for Week 7 against the Raiders on Sunday, and Coleman's role on offense would shrink if Moore is cleared to return.

headline: Coleman secured six of seven targets for 116 yards and a touchdown in the Bills' 29-26 loss to the Patriots on Sunday.
story: DJ Moore went down in the first half with a shoulder injury, opening up plenty of opportunity in the Bills' air attack. Coleman almost fully maximized his additional targets, recording a team-high yardage figure while finishing second in both receptions and targets. Coleman's first two pro seasons were marked by inconsistency, but the third-year wideout has secured 14 of 16 targets for 217 yards and a touchdown over the first four games of 2026, and 10 of his catches have resulted in first downs. Coleman's 34-yard touchdown grab Sunday also would have delivered the game-winning points had Drake Maye not mounted a successful drive on the ensuing possession, and Coleman could remain in an elevated role during a Week 5 road matchup against the Rams on Monday night, Oct. 12, if Moore is sidelined for that contest.

headline: Coleman (ankle) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Patriots.
story: Coleman was DNP on Wednesday but got in a pair of limited practices Thursday and Friday and is ready to go for Sunday's divisional matchup. Coleman has made the most of his limited opportunities in a complementary role early on this season, securing eight of nine targets for 101 yards.

headline: Coleman (ankle) was a limited participant in Thursday's practice.
story: A spectator for the Bills' first Week 4 practice Wednesday, Coleman was able to take a step forward in activity a day later. The third-year wideout will likely need to upgrade to full activity to avoid carrying a designation into Sunday's game against the Patriots, but at this stage in the week, he appears to be trending toward playing.

headline: Coleman (ankle) did not practice Wednesday.
story: Coleman dealt with the ankle injury in practice last week and was listed as questionable for Week 3 before suiting up and playing just 48.5 percent of the offensive snaps against the Chargers. He turned two targets into one catch for 37 yards. If Coleman is unable to play Sunday against the Patriots, Joshua Palmer would be in line for increased snaps.

headline: Coleman saw two targets and recorded a 37-yard catch during the Bills' 24-16 win over the Chargers on Sunday.
story: Coleman's practice reps during Week 3 prep were limited by an ankle injury, but he was cleared to play and ended up handling 32 of 66 offensive snaps (48.5 percent), third most among Bills wide receivers behind Khalil Shakir (48) and DJ Moore (42). Coleman was responsible for his team's longest play of the game late in the second quarter, setting up a one-yard TD for Josh Allen on the next play. Coleman is capable of making big plays, but it's hard to rely on him for consistent production when he's behind Moore, Shakir, tight end Dalton Kincaid and running back James Cook in the pecking order for targets. The Bills wrap up a three-game homestand this Sunday in an AFC East showdown against the Patriots, whose defense gave up 35 points (including three passing touchdowns) to the Jaguars in a Week 3 loss.

headline: Coleman (ankle) is listed as active for Sunday's game against the Chargers.
story: It was reported earlier Sunday that Coleman was expected to suit up for Week 3, and he will indeed do so. Coleman was considered a game-time call for Sunday's contest, so it's not clear if he will be at full speed. However, he -- as well as DJ Moore and the rest of Buffalo's regular pass catchers -- will all be in uniform for Week 3.

headline: Coleman (ankle), who is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Chargers, is expected to play, Cameron Wolfe of NFL Network reports.
story: After Coleman sat out practices Wednesday and Thursday before returning to the field as a limited participant Friday, head coach Joe Brady told Katherine Fitzgerald of The Buffalo News that the wideout would be a game-time decision leading up to Sunday's contest. The third-year player has apparently made positive strides in his recovery from the ankle injury following Friday's practice, and barring a setback, he should be cleared to play ahead of the 1 p.m. ET kickoff. Coleman has recorded seven receptions for 64 yards on seven targets through the Bills' first two games of the season, and he could be in store for more volume if fellow wideout DJ Moore (shoulder) -- whom Brady also termed as a game-time decision -- ends up sitting out Sunday.

headline: Coleman (ankle) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game versus the Chargers.
story: After sitting out the Bills' first two Week 3 practices due to an ankle injury, Coleman was back on the field Friday and logged an official limited session to wrap up the week. Head coach Joe Brady told Katherine Fitzgerald of The Buffalo News that both Coleman and fellow WR DJ Moore (shoulder) will be game-time decisions, so the statuses of both players may not be known until approximately 90 minutes before Sunday's 1:00 p.m. ET kickoff.

headline: Coleman (ankle) wasn't spotted at the start of Thursday's practice, Joe Buscaglia of The Athletic reports.
story: Both Coleman and DJ Moore (shoulder) appear to be sitting out practice Thursday, leaving Khalil Shakir, Joshua Palmer and Skyler Bell as Buffalo's only healthy wide receivers on the active roster. Coleman likely will need to practice in some capacity Friday to give himself a chance to suit up for Sunday's game against the Chargers.

headline: Coleman didn't practice Wednesday due to an ankle injury.
story: DJ Moore was believed to be the Bills wide receiver dealing with a health concern this week after he suffered an AC joint sprain last Thursday against the Lions. Instead, Moore was a limited participant Wednesday, while Coleman didn't log any practice reps at all to kick off Week 3 prep. Coleman's status thus bears watching Thursday and Friday to see whether or not he's trending toward an absence Sunday versus the Chargers.

headline: Coleman brought in all six targets for 63 yards in the Bills' 41-31 win over the Lions on Thursday.
story: Coleman benefited from the late second-quarter exit of DJ Moore (shoulder), finishing the game second in receptions and receiving yards for the Bills while also tying for runner-up status in targets. The oft-maligned 2024 second-round pick encouragingly flashed steady hands as well throughout the night, and Coleman will be in line to continue in an enhanced role in a Week 3 home matchup against the Chargers on Sunday, Sept. 27 if Moore is forced to sit out the contest.

headline: Coleman caught his lone target for one yard in the Bills' 36-31 win over the Texans on Sunday.
story: Buffalo continued to use a rotation at wide receiver to open the 2026 campaign. While DJ Moore paced the group with 26 routes on Josh Allen's 32 dropbacks, Khalil Shakir (20), Coleman (19) and Joshua Palmer (13) fell in line behind him. Between Coleman and Palmer, it was the latter who had the big play, recording what proved to be the game-winning 34-yard touchdown catch with 1:37 left in the fourth quarter. Coleman was targeted on the subsequent failed two-point conversion, and he'll likely need an injury ahead of him to have any fantasy appeal.

headline: Coleman (foot) is not listed on the Bills' Week 1 injury report Wednesday.
story: Coleman was in a walking boot last month but returned to practice last week and is ready for Week 1 against the Texans. Listed as a starter on the unofficial depth chart, Coleman will be part of the rotation at wide receiver for Buffalo. He doesn't carry much redraft fantasy value and is a better best-ball selection in an offense that again has a lot of mouths to feed.

headline: Coleman (foot) is listed as one of three starting receivers on the Bills' unofficial depth chart for Sunday's season opener versus the Texans, Joe Buscaglia of The Athletic reports.
story: While DJ Moore and Khalil Shakir are secure as Buffalo's top two wideouts, Coleman appears to be ahead of Joshua Palmer for the No. 3 spot. After averaging 9.8 yards per target as a rookie in 2024, Coleman dropped all the way down to 6.8 per game during his sophomore season and also drew the ire of the coaching staff for his lack of professionalism, leading to him being a healthy scratch on four occasions. Coleman received a clean slate entering 2026, and after a strong showing during minicamp, he continued to make a positive impression in training camp before spraining his right foot in an Aug. 18 preseason game. The injury doesn't appear to be a long-term concern, and if he can return to full practice at some point this week, Coleman could handle a notable role in the passing game in the season opener.

headline: Coleman (right foot/toe) was present at Tuesday's practice, Joe Buscaglia of The Athletic reports.
story: Coleman sustained a sprained right foot/toe in the Bills' preseason opener Aug. 15, but he ditched his low walking boot as of last Thursday and now appears set to mix back into drills. The extent of his activity Tuesday isn't known, but he still has nearly two weeks to get healthy ahead of a Week 1 road matchup with the Texans on Sunday, Sept. 13.

headline: Coleman (right foot/toe) isn't in uniform for Thursday's preseason game against the Steelers, but he wasn't wearing a walking boot, Alex Brasky of SI.com reports.
story: Coleman has been tending to a sprained right foot/toe that he sustained in the Bills' exhibition opener, which forced him to don a low walking boot since then. Shedding the boot is a positive sign in his recovery effort, but Coleman will join Khalil Shakir (undisclosed) and Tyrell Shavers (knee, active/PUP) as injured Buffalo wide receivers that won't suit up Thursday. Coleman will turn his focus to getting completely healthy for the team's regular-season opener Sunday, Sept. 13 at Houston.
