He exhibited a visible limp in the aftermath, but he later told Kelsey Conway of The Cincinnati Enquirer that it was a "little hyperextension," and he could have resumed practicing. Chase will attempt to put the issue behind him ahead of a Week 1 matchup with the Buccaneers on Sunday, Sept. 13.

headline: Chase (knee) is not participating in Wednesday's practice, Ben Baby of ESPN.com reports.
story: Chase downplayed the injury that forced him from Tuesday's session, but he will get at least one day to rest and recover. The report notes that Chase "was not sporting any protective equipment," which backs up his stance that he is dealing only with a minor setback.

headline: Chase (knee) said Tuesday that he could play in a game Wednesday after exiting Tuesday's practice early, Kelsey Conway of the Cincinnati Enquirer reports.
story: Chase has spent Tuesday afternoon downplaying his hyperextended knee, so this seems like it will be a non-issue moving forward after he came down awkwardly at the end of practice. The star wide receiver is a cinch top-five fantasy pick as Joe Burrow's alpha wideout.

headline: Chase downplayed his knee injury Tuesday, saying it was a "little hyperextension," and he could've kept practicing, Kelsey Conway of the Cincinnati Enquirer reports.
story: Chase came up limping at the tail end of Tuesday's session when he jumped for a deep ball and landed awkwardly. He immediately left the field and was tended to by the training staff before shooing them away and remaining on the sidelines for the remainder of practice. It sounds like Chase will be fine well in time for the Bengals' regular-season opener in a little less than three weeks.

headline: Chase (knee) limped off the field at Tuesday's practice after landing awkwardly while attempting to reel in a deep ball, Jay Morrison of SI.com reports.
story: Chase was favoring his left knee after the play in question, but he was able to walk to the sideline under his own power with trainers, per Charlie Clifford of NBC 5 Cincinnati. Potentially a major development for the Bengals offense, Chase's status should receive some clarity after Tuesday's session.

headline: Cook (ankle) is active for Sunday's game against Miami.
story: Cook didn't play in Week 4 against Jacksonville but will return Sunday versus Miami, likely resulting in fewer defensive snaps for PJ Jules.

headline: Cook (ankle) is listed as questionable against the Dolphins on Sunday, Paul Dehner Jr. of The Athletic reports.
story: Cook has a chance to return from a one-game absence due to an ankle injury, and he ended Week 5 prep on a positive note with a full practice Friday. If he's cleared to play against Miami, then PJ Jules would revert to a depth role at safety behind Cook and Jordan Battle.

headline: Cook (ankle) was a limited practice participant Thursday.
story: Cook hurt his ankle in Week 3 against Pittsburgh and was unable to suit up this past Sunday versus Jacksonville. He didn't practice Wednesday, but his ability to participate in a limited fashion Thursday gives Cook at least a chance of suiting up in Week 5 against Miami. He'll likely carry an injury designation into the weekend unless he's able to practice in full Friday.

headline: Cook (ankle) is inactive for Sunday's Week 4 tilt against Jacksonville.
story: Cook suffered an ankle injury last Sunday versus Pittsburgh. Though he was able to re-enter that contest, he was limited in all three practices this week and has ultimately been ruled out for Sunday's matchup. Kyle Dugger (quadriceps) is also out Week 4, so PJ Jules is likely to step into a starting role.

headline: Cook (ankle) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Jaguars.
story: Cook injured his ankle during the Bengals' Week 3 loss to the Steelers, though he was able to return to that contest. He was a limited participant in all three practices during Week 4 prep, and if he's unable to play against Jacksonville, then PJ Jules would likely start at safety alongside Jordan Battle, seeing as Kyle Dugger (quadriceps) has already been ruled out.

headline: Cook (ankle) has returned to Sunday's game against the Steelers, Jay Morrison of SI.com reports.
story: Cook left in the first half of Sunday's game due to an ankle injury, but he was back on the field for the second half after being cleared by medical staff.

headline: Cook (ankle) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Steelers.
story: Cook suffered an ankle injury in the first half. If he can't return to the AFC North clash versus Pittsburgh, Kyle Dugger will be in line for a boost in snaps.

headline: Cook (undisclosed) participated during the Bengals' training camp practice Tuesday, Ben Baby of ESPN.com reports.
story: Cook has missed time after suffering an apparent hamstring injury earlier in August, but it now looks like he's back in football shape. Despite whether he plays in Friday's preseason game at Philadelphia, it seems like he's trending toward being available for Week 1 of the regular season, barring any setbacks.

headline: Hill (Achilles) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice, Jay Morrison of SI.com reports.
story: Hill missed three consecutive games with an Achilles injury he suffered in the Bengals' Week 1 win over the Buccaneers. Wednesday's full session is the first the defensive tackle has logged since sustaining the injury, meaning there is a strong chance Hill will be able to suit up for Sunday's game against the Dolphins.

headline: Hill (Achilles) is inactive for Sunday's clash against the Jaguars.
story: Hill will miss his third straight game after suffering an Achilles injury in Week 1. He did manage a limited practice session Friday after beginning the week with a pair of DNPs, so he may be ready to start ramping up toward a return. Kris Jenkins may continue to log more defensive reps Sunday in Hill's stead.

headline: Hill (Achilles) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Steelers.
story: Hill drew the doubtful tag after not practicing during Week 3 prep, and the veteran defensive tackle will not be on the Bengals' active roster for Sunday's AFC North tilt. His next chance to play is Week 4 against the Jaguars on Sunday, Oct. 4.

headline: Hill (Achilles) is inactive for Sunday's Week 2 matchup against the Texans.
story: Hill was on the field for 41 percent of Cincinnati's defensive snaps in Week 1 against Tampa Bay but didn't record a tackle or any counting stat. He only appeared in a limited fashion on Thursday during the practice week, which set the stage for his inactive status. He'll look to return Week 3 against Pittsburgh.

headline: The Bengals activated Hill (undisclosed) from the active/PUP list Saturday after he passed a physical.
story: Hill opened training camp on the PUP list while recovering from an unspecified injury. He's been given the green light to return to practice and is on track to play in the Bengals' next preseason game, which takes place Saturday, Aug. 22 against the Bears. Hill has suited up for the Bengals in each of the last five years and is coming off a 2025 campaign in which he logged 66 tackles (29 solo), including 4.0 sacks, across 17 regular-season games.

headline: Lawrence logged four tackles (three solo), including 2.0 sacks, in the Bengals' 30-27 loss to the Steelers on Sunday.
story: The prominent offseason addition to the Bengals' defensive line dominated in Sunday's game, showing why he commanded the 10th overall pick in the 2026 Draft as trade capital. Lawrence sacked Aaron Rodgers two times in the contest and accumulated another two tackles, anchoring the middle of the Bengals' 4-3 defensive front.

headline: Carter posted 11 tackles (five solo) and one pass defense during Sunday's 22-17 loss to the Jaguars.
story: Carter logged double-digit tackles for the first time this season, and his 11 stops were his most in a game since Week 12 of the 2025 campaign (16). The second-year linebacker is up to 30 tackles (14 solo), including 0.5 sacks, two pass defenses and one forced fumble through four regular-season games and has played every single defensive snap in that span.

headline: Carter registered five total tackles (two solo) during Sunday's 20-6 win over the Texans.
story: Carter was able to finish tied for fourth on the team in takedowns with cornerback DJ Turner, and one of the former's tackles was for a loss. The linebacker has played every defensive snap with the Bengals this season, and he figures to be on track for a big year if his workload remains that high.

headline: Knight finished Sunday's 22-17 loss to the Jaguars with six tackles (three solo).
story: Linebacker Barrett Carter led the Bengals with 11 total tackles Sunday, with Knight finishing as the team's runner-up in that category. Knight's 45 defensive snaps (73.8 percent) were his fewest of the season after the second-year pro played at least 89.5 percent of the Bengals' defensive snaps in each of his first three games. He's up to 34 tackles (14 solo) and a scoop-and-score on the year.

headline: Knight made nine tackles (two solo) in the Bengals' 30-27 loss to the Steelers on Sunday.
story: Knight played 56 defensive snaps in the contest, good for 90 percent of the Bengals' defensive plays. The weak-side linebacker led the team in tackles but was unable to do much more in a close loss.

headline: Knight recorded 12 total tackles (four solo) during Sunday's 20-6 win over Houston.
story: Knight was able to lead the team in takedowns as he continued his hot start to the season versus the Texans. The linebacker has now registered 19 total tackles (nine solo) and a fumble recovery that he returned for a touchdown over two contests to open the 2026 campaign.

headline: Knight totaled seven tackles (five solo) and returned a fumble for a touchdown during the Bengals' win over Tampa Bay on Sunday.
story: Knight got off to a strong start this season, as he managed to score his first career touchdown while finishing tied for fourth on the team in tackles. The 2025 second-round pick recorded 106 tackles (58 solo), including 3.0 sacks, across 17 games and will look to keep producing next week against the Texans.

headline: Tinsley caught three of his seven targets for 49 yards in the Bengals' 22-17 loss to the Jaguars on Sunday.
story: Tinsley's seven targets were fourth most among Bengals pass catchers behind Tee Higgins' (groin) 16, Chase Brown's 11 and Dohnte Meyers' nine. Tinsley stepped up after Ja'Marr Chase exited the contest with a concussion. Tinsley signed with the active roster Sept. 29 and likely will remain on it while the team deals with extensive injuries to the wide receiver corps.

headline: The Bengals signed Tinsley off the Texans' practice squad to the active roster Tuesday.
story: The Bengals needed to replenish their depth at wide receiver due to the injury absences of Andrei Iosivas (thumb, IR) and rookie fourth-rounder Colbie Young (knee), the latter of whom has already been ruled out for Week 4 against the Jaguars. Tinsley appeared in 17 regular-season games for the Bengals in 2025, finishing with an 8-117-2 receiving line on 24 targets, though he joined the Texans' practice squad Sept. 1 after failing to make Cincinnati's 53-man roster at the end of training camp. Now that he's back with the Bengals, Tinsley will contribute both on special teams and in a rotational role on offense.

headline: Tinsley signed with Houston's practice squad Monday, Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston reports.
story: The fourth-year wideout played in all 17 games for the Bengals in 2025, stringing together an 8-116-2 line on 24 targets while handling a depth role in the receiving corps. Tinsley was unable to win a spot on the Bengals' roster coming out of training camp, but he could have a clearer path to seeing playing time in Houston at some point in 2026 with Jayden Higgins (knee) out for the season and Tank Dell (knee) set to miss at least the team's first four games.

headline: Tinsley was waived by the Bengals on Sunday, Charlie Clifford of NBC 5 Cincinnati reports.
story: The wide receiver caught eight passes for 116 yards and two touchdowns for the Bengals in 2025. He also played on 123 special-teams snaps and agreed to a one-year extension with the team in January, but he fell short of the 53-man roster for 2026 after a competition with rookie fourth-round pick Colbie Young and former Canadian Football League player Dohnte Meyers. Tinsley has NFL experience and could find a home on the practice squad of either Cincinnati or another team.

headline: Turner (hamstring) does not carry an injury designation into Sunday's game versus Tampa Bay.
story: Turner was a limited participant at practice again Friday, but it looks like he'll be okay to suit up in Week 1 anyway. He projects for a huge role in Cincinnati's secondary in 2026, the final year of his rookie contract.

headline: Turner was limited in practice Thursday due to a hamstring issue, Jay Morrison of SI.com reports.
story: Turner wasn't listed on Cincinnati's practice report Wednesday, so he may have picked up the hamstring injury during practice. Bengals fans (and fantasy managers who roster any of Tampa Bay's passing-game pieces) may want to keep a keen eye on Friday's practice report and injury designations to get an idea of Turner's chance of suiting up Sunday. Should he not be able to play, Bucs QB Baker Mayfield, along with wideouts Emeka Egbuka and Chris Godwin, could get a bump in projected value.

headline: Sampson (knee) was a non-participant in Wednesday's practice.
story: Despite being designated for return from injured reserve earlier Wednesday, Sampson didn't end up logging any reps after having his 21-day practice window opened. Prior to the Browns' first Week 6 practice, head coach Todd Monken told Scott Petrak of the Elyria Chronicle-Telegram that Sampson has a chance at being activated from injured reserve ahead of Sunday's game against the Ravens, but the second-year back would likely need to put in a full workout Thursday or Friday to make that a reality.

headline: The Browns designated Sampson (knee) for return from injured reserve Wednesday, Mary Kay Cabot of The Cleveland Plain Dealer reports.
story: The transaction clears the way for Sampson to practice Wednesday and opens a 21-day window for the Browns to evaluate him for a return to the 53-man roster. The second-year back has been sidelined since sustaining the left knee injury during the Browns' Week 1 loss to the Jaguars, but head coach Todd Monken suggested that Sampson could have a shot at playing Sunday versus the Ravens, per Scott Petrak of the Elyria Chronicle-Telegram. Sampson will likely need to turn in at least one full practice over the next three days for the Browns to feel comfortable activating him from injured reserve ahead of their Week 6 matchup.

headline: Head coach Todd Monken said Monday that there is a "possibility" that the Browns open the 21-day practice window for Sampson (knee) this week, Daniel Oyefusi of ESPN.com reports.
story: Sampson was placed on injured reserve in mid-September due to a left knee injury he sustained in Week 1 against the Jaguars. Monken opened the door for Sampson to be designated to return from IR during Week 6 prep, though his practice participation over the coming days ultimately will determine whether he's ready to play against the Ravens on Sunday. Sampson's potential return could be an important one for the Browns, given that Quinshon Judkins (foot) and Raheim Sanders (hip) both left this past Sunday's 17-12 loss to the Jets due to their respective injuries.

headline: Sampson (knee) was placed on injured reserve Tuesday.
story: It's unclear exactly how much time Sampson will miss. He is expected back this season, per Mary Kay Cabot of The Cleveland Plain Dealer, but his placement on IR means he will miss at least the next four games. Jaleel McLaughlin was brought up from the practice squad, and both he and Raheim Sanders -- who played 18 snaps on offense and got four touches Sunday after Sampson's exit -- will work behind starter Quinshon Judkins.

headline: Sampson (knee) is expected to miss "significant time," Jeremy Fowler of ESPN.com reports.
story: Sampson hurt his left knee in Sunday's Week 1 loss to Jacksonville and was on crutches while wearing a brace after the game. It appears that further evaluation on the running back has concluded that Sampson is dealing with a severe injury. It's not yet clear exactly how much time he'll miss, though there's certainly a chance he'll end up on IR. Raheim Sanders likely will take on a bigger role in Sampson's absence, and Jaleel McLaughlin could be summoned from the practice squad.

headline: Coach Todd Monken said Monday the team is still evaluating the severity of Sampson's knee injury, Daniel Oyefusi of ESPN.com reports.
story: Monken said more information will be known Wednesday, which would suggest he's playing coy since the Browns aren't required to provide any update until an injury report needs to be released Wednesday. Sampson was on crutches after Sunday's loss to the Jaguars, so he's likely looking at some missed time at least. Quinshon Judkins and Raheim Sanders handled backfield duties with Sampson sidelined.

headline: Sampson was on crutches and wearing a brace on the left knee he injured during Sunday's loss to Jacksonville, Mary Kay Cabot of The Cleveland Plain Dealer reports.
story: Sampson was hurt in the first quarter. He was initially deemed questionable but was eventually downgraded to out after being evaluated in the medical tent and the locker room. Quinshon Judkins (12 carries) and Raheim Sanders (one carry) were the only Browns running backs to log any totes during the Week 1 defeat. Sampson is slated to undergo further testing Monday, per Daniel Oyefusi of ESPN.com.

headline: Sampson (knee) has been downgraded to out for Sunday's game against the Jaguars.
story: Sampson was initially deemed questionable to return after injuring his knee in the first quarter, but after making a visit to the medical tent on the sideline followed by two trips to the locker room, the Browns determined that his day is over, per Daniel Oyefusi of ESPN.com. His absence leaves Cleveland with Raheim Sanders as its lone backup behind starter Quinshon Judkins for the remainder of the game. Sampson didn't receive any touches on offense but gained 64 yards on two kickoff returns prior to his departure.

headline: Sampson sustained a knee injury in the first quarter of Sunday's game against the Jaguars and is considered questionable to return, Mary Kay Cabot of The Cleveland Plain Dealer reports.
story: Sampson didn't receive any touches on offense but returned two kickoffs for 64 yards before exiting the contest. The second-year running back headed to the locker room and will be evaluated further before the Browns decide whether he'll be able to return to the game.

headline: Sampson was rested for the Browns' 37-13 win over the Patriots in their Aug. 27 preseason finale.
story: Cleveland held both of their top two backs -- Quinshon Judkins and Sampson -- out for the third game of the preseason to open up more playing time for other running backs to stake claims to roster spots. Judkins is locked in as the Browns' lead runner heading into their Week 1 matchup with the Jaguars, but Sampson should have a consistent role as a weapon on passing downs. Sampson proved to be adept as a pass catcher during his 2025 rookie campaign, drawing 40 targets on just 249 snaps while producing a 33-271-2 receiving line. He was much less productive as a runner, however, averaging just 2.7 yards per carry on 65 totes.

headline: Sampson carried the ball four times for six yards and caught both his targets for 43 yards in Saturday's 34-10 preseason loss to the Bears.
story: The second-year running back ended up leading Cleveland in receiving yards on the day, with his 43-yard reception from Deshaun Watson in the second quarter setting up the team's only TD. Sampson is firmly behind Quinshon Judkins on the backfield depth chart, but the 2025 fourth-round pick should still have a role on passing downs after posting a 33-271-2 line on 40 targets over 15 regular-season games as a rookie.

headline: Browns head coach Todd Monken said Wednesday that Jenkins has cleared the league's concussion protocol, Tom Withers of The Associated Press reports.
story: Jenkins practiced fully Wednesday, putting him on track to play in Sunday's game against the Jets. He missed the Browns' Week 4 win over the Steelers while recovering from the concussion.

headline: Jenkins (concussion) is officially listed as out for Thursday's game versus the Steelers.
story: Jenkins was unable to practice during the week after entering concussion protocol, and he'll now spend at least one game on the sidelines as he recovers. In his stead, Luke Wypler projects to start at center in Week 4.

headline: Jenkins didn't participate at practice Tuesday due to a concussion, Daniel Oyefusi of ESPN.com reports.
story: Jenkins entered the concussion protocol in the wake of Sunday's 21-18 win over the Panthers. With no listed participation in the Browns' first two Week 4 sessions, Jenkins could have a tough time clearing the protocol ahead of Thursday's game against the Steelers. If Jenkins can't play Thursday, Luke Wypler would likely be in line to start at center.

headline: Jenkins (back) does not carry an injury designation into Sunday's game against the Buccaneers.
story: Jenkins was limited by a back injury in each of the first two practices of the week. He's been given the green light to play Sunday after logging a full practice Friday, and Jenkins will once again serve as the Browns' starting center while rookie fifth-rounder Parker Brailsford (thumb) provides depth at the position.

headline: Jenkins (back) was a limited participant in practice Thursday, Scott Petrak of the Elyria Chronicle-Telegram reports.
story: The starting center was limited Wednesday as well. If the issue is serious enough to keep Jenkins out of Sunday's game against the Buccaneers, Parker Brailsford (thumb) and Luke Wypler are in line to step in.

headline: Delpit logged six tackles (four solo) and one pass defensed in the Browns' 27-24 win over the Steelers on Thursday.
story: Delpit played 62 defensive snaps in the contest, good for 97 percent of the Browns' total defensive plays. The strong safety's six tackles were his most in a game so far this season.

headline: Delpit (shoulder) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice session.
story: Delpit was able to play through a shoulder issue during the Browns' 21-18 win over the Panthers on Sunday, and the seventh-year pro will do the same for Thursday's AFC North clash against the Steelers. He's played every single defensive snap through three regular-season games, accumulating 12 tackles (eight solo), including 1.0 sacks and one pass defense in that span.

headline: Delpit (shoulder) was estimated as a limited participant in Monday's practice, Adam Caplan of SiriusXM NFL Radio reports.
story: Delpit played all 74 defensive snaps for the Browns in Sunday's 21-18 win over the Panthers despite battling through a shoulder injury. The strong safety suited up after only logging limited sessions in the Browns' Week 3 prep, and Delpit may be on track to mirror that participation pattern leading into Thursday's Week 4 matchup against the Steelers.

headline: Delpit (shoulder) is active for Sunday's game against the Panthers, Kelsey Russo of the Browns' official site reports.
story: Delpit expressed optimism Saturday that he would be available for Week 3 after working through a shoulder issue during practice, and the veteran safety has been given the green light to play. The 2020 second-rounder has eight tackles (six solo), including 1.0 sacks, and one pass defense through two regular-season games.

headline: Delpit (shoulder) said he will play in Sunday's game against the Panthers, Scott Petrak of the Elyria Chronicle-Telegram reports.
story: Delpit said he feels good enough to take the field in Sunday's game. The strong safety has been dealing with a shoulder injury he likely suffered in the Browns' Week 2 win over the Buccaneers. Delpit's presence means rookie second-rounder Emmanuel McNeil-Warren likely won't see many snaps in the contest.

headline: Delpit (shoulder) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Panthers, Zac Jackson of The Athletic reports.
story: Delpit was a limited participant in all three practices this past week while tending to a shoulder issue. If he's unable to play against Carolina, then rookie second-rounder Emmanuel McNeil-Warren would be the top candidate to start at safety alongside Ronnie Hickman. Delpit has eight tackles (six solo), including 1.0 sacks, and one pass defense through two regular-season games.

headline: Graham (knee/ankle) has been ruled out ahead of Sunday's game against the Jets, Daniel Oyefusi of ESPN.com reports.
story: Graham sprained his MCL in the Browns' Week 4 win over the Steelers. The defensive tackle has not practiced since sustaining the injury and thus will not play in Sunday's contest. Adin Huntington is set to start at defensive tackle opposite Maliek Collins for the matchup with the Jets.

headline: Graham underwent an MRI on Friday that revealed he sustained an MCL and ankle sprain in Thursday night's game, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
story: Graham avoided a devastating injury in Thursday night's game. The team leader in sacks is expected to remain week-to-week as he begins his recovery process, per Scott Petrak of the Elyria Chronicle-Telegram. Adin Huntington could see additional reps opposite Jared Verse while Graham is sidelined.

headline: Graham exited the Cleveland locker room on crutches and with a brace on his left knee following Thursday's 27-24 win over Pittsburgh, Chris Easterling of the Akron Beacon Journal reports.
story: Graham was hurt early in the first half during a Pittsburgh running play. The 2025 first-round draft pick was initially deemed questionable before being ruled out shortly after halftime. Graham's need to use crutches and a brace following the victory isn't a promising sign, though the Browns' medical staff will ultimately give him a diagnosis upon further examination.

headline: Graham (knee) has been ruled out for the remainder of Thursday's Week 4 matchup versus Pittsburgh, Chris Easterling of the Akron Beacon Journal reports.
story: Graham suffered a knee injury early in the first half and was ruled out shortly after halftime. The second-year pro didn't record any defensive statistics prior to his exit. Mike Hall suffered an ankle injury in the contest and is questionable to return, leaving Maliek Collins and Adin Huntington as Cleveland's only defensive tackles.

headline: Graham (knee) is questionable to return to Thursday's game against the Steelers.
story: Graham suffered a knee injury early in the contest and was shown limping to the locker room with the training staff. If Graham doesn't return Thursday, Adin Huntington may be more involved the rest of the way.

headline: Graham logged seven tackles (four solo), including 2.0 sacks, in the Browns' 21-18 win over the Panthers on Sunday.
story: Graham played 53 defensive snaps in the contest and notched two of the three sacks on quarterback Bryce Young. The second-year defensive tackle out of Michigan totaled 0.5 sacks throughout 17 games in 2025, so Sunday's production was easily a career high for the young player. Graham is up to 4.0 sacks through three regular-season games in 2026, leading all defensive tackles.

headline: Concepcion (concussion) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice.
story: Just three days after sustaining a concussion when he was on the receiving end of a helmet-to-helmet hit from the Jets' Minkah Fitzpatrick, Concepcion was able to make enough progress through the five-step protocol to open Week 6 prep on the field, albeit in a limited fashion. He'll have two more chances to upgrade to full participation and will then need to receive clearance from an independent neurologist before being removed from the protocol. If Concepcion can't play Sunday against the Ravens, Jerry Jeudy and Isaiah Bond would be in line for added reps alongside Denzel Boston (foot) in two- and three-receiver sets.

headline: Concepcion is progressing well in his recovery from a concussion and is set to practice Wednesday, Mary Kay Cabot of The Cleveland Plain Dealer reports.
story: Though he remains in the five-step concussion protocol after being knocked out of this past Sunday's 17-12 loss to the Jets following a helmet-to-helmet hit from safety Minkah Fitzpatrick, Concepcion's ability to practice in any fashion to begin Week 6 prep is an encouraging sign. The rookie wideout will likely need to upgrade to full practice participation by the end of the week in addition to gaining clearance from an independent neurologist in order to have a shot at playing Sunday against the Ravens.

headline: Concepcion has entered the NFL's concussion protocol, Daniel Oyefusi of ESPN.com reported Sunday.
story: Concepcion sustained a concussion in the Browns' 17-12 loss to the Jets on Sunday after taking a hard hit from Minkah Fitzpatrick. The rookie wideout will now have to clear the NFL's five-step concussion protocol before he can return to game action. Concepcion's status for a Week 6 home divisional matchup against the Ravens will bear monitoring over the upcoming practice week.

headline: Concepcion (head) has been ruled out for the rest of Sunday's game at the Jets.
story: Concepcion took a hit from Jets safety Minkah Fitzpatrick early during Week 5 action and hit his head on the turf, after which the rookie wide receiver went directly to the locker room before the Browns made a ruling on his status. In Concepcion's absence, Denzel Boston will handle WR1 duties, with Jerry Jeudy, Isaiah Bond and Malachi Corley filling in behind him.

headline: Concepcion secured five of eight targets for 64 yards and returned two punts for 10 yards in the Browns' 27-24 win over the Steelers on Thursday.
story: Concepcion and fellow rookie Denzel Boston continued to spark the Browns' air attack Thursday, and the former finished second in receptions and receiving yards while setting the pace in targets. Concepcion's catch and yardage totals also qualified as new career highs, and the productive night served as a welcome bounce-back effort after the rookie first-round pick had been held to 2-9-0 receiving line in the Week 3 win over the Panthers. He should continue to garner plenty of Deshaun Watson's attention in a Week 5 road matchup against the Jets on Sunday, Oct. 11.

headline: Concepcion finished Sunday's 21-18 victory versus Carolina with two catches (on nine targets) for nine yards. He also returned one punt for one yard.
story: Concepcion actually tied tight end Harold Fannin for the team lead with nine targets, but the rookie wideout managed to haul in just two of those looks. His receptions went for five and four yards, continuing what has become a trend, as he's averaging a meager 6.7 yards per reception so far this season. The target share indicates that the Browns want Concepcion to be an integral part of the passing game, but so far he doesn't seem to be clicking with QB Deshaun Watson.

headline: Concepcion caught all six targets for 28 yards in Sunday's 23-19 win over the Bucs. He added one rushing attempt for minus-6 yards.
story: Concepcion's six targets tied Harold Fannin for second on the team, finishing one behind Denzel Boston, who proved again to be the big-play threat for the Browns, finishing with a 5-95-1 receiving line. Concepcion is running the majority of his routes from the slot, but his average depth of target was a microscopic 1.8 yards Sunday. It's going to be difficult to produce big yards when catching the ball basically at the line of scrimmage. Through two games, Concepcion has 10 catches for 71 scoreless yards on 11 targets. He gets a boost in PPR formats as a WR4/5 headed into next Sunday's date with the Panthers.

headline: Concepcion caught four of his five targets for 43 yards in Sunday's 34-10 loss to the Jaguars.
story: While Concepcion paced the team with his five targets, he ran just 20 routes on Deshaun Watson's 30 dropbacks, good for fourth on the Browns behind Denzel Boston (30), Jerry Jeudy (25) and Harold Fannin (24). It's going to be very difficult for this lackluster Cleveland offense to support any pass catchers as every-week fantasy starters. Concepcion will be a WR4/5 for next Sunday's road date with the Bucs.

headline: Browns coach Todd Monken said Friday that Concepcion will handle all of the punt returns Sunday against Jacksonville, Scott Petrak of the Elyria Chronicle-Telegram reports.
story: Concepcion also figures to be one of the team's top offensive weapons, locked in for a top-three role alongside presumed starters Jerry Jeudy and Denzel Boston. The Browns also have TE Harold Fannin and RBs Quinshon Judkins and Dylan Sampson in the mix for short-area targets, but Monken seems intent on getting the ball into Concepcion's hands, one way or another.

headline: Concepcion told reporters after Wednesday's practice that he's looking forward to carrying his strong play in training camp into the regular season, starting with the Browns' Week 1 clash against the Jaguars on Sunday, Sept. 13, Chris Easterling of the Akron Beacon Journal reports.
story: "Seeing that these coaches have trust built up in me to put me in different type of situations, I would say that it only makes me more excited for Week 1," Concepcion shared with reporters Wednesday. Concepcion's lone preseason appearance was against the Bears on Aug. 15, but he looked good in that game and finished with three catches (on four targets) for 27 yards while adding a 14-yard rushing touchdown and a 31-yard punt return. The Texas A&M product was one of the standout players for the Browns in training camp, and the rookie first-rounder has enough trust from his coaching staff to be an immediate contributor on offense. Concepcion, fellow rookie Denzel Boston, veteran Jerry Jeudy, tight end Harold Fannin and running back Quinshon Judkins figure to be the key playmakers for the Browns this season, with Deshaun Watson manning the offense, at least to begin the campaign.

headline: Concepcion caught three of four targets for 27 yards and took his only carry 14 yards for a touchdown in Saturday's 34-10 preseason loss to the Bears.
story: The rookie speedster just managed to stay in bounds and squeak into the end zone on an end-around in the second quarter. Concepcion, the 24th overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, dealt with a minor shoulder issue last week, but it didn't seem to bother him in the first preseason action of his career. He's expected to be a key part of the passing game alongside veteran Jerry Jeudy and fellow rookie Denzel Boston, but Concepcion's usage Saturday is a good sign that he could see extra touches on the ground as well.

headline: Collins (quadriceps) was activated from the active/PUP list Monday.
story: Collins was able to pass a physical after missing the entirety of training camp to this point while recovering from a quadriceps injury that he suffered in December. The defensive lineman is now eligible to return to practice at any point, and he appears to be on track to be ready to go for Week 1 against the Jaguars on Sept. 13.

headline: Barnett and the Browns agreed to a one-year contract worth up to $5.5 million Sunday, Jeremy Fowler of ESPN.com reports.
story: The move fortifies the Browns' depth at defensive end after Alex Wright (Achilles) was placed on season-ending injured reserve. Barnett appeared in 17 regular-season games for the Texans in 2025, finishing with 21 tackles (13 solo), including 5.0 sacks. With Wright on IR, Barnett figures to serve in a rotational role at defensive end for the Browns behind starters Jared Verse and Isaiah McGuire.

headline: Boston was listed as a limited participant in Wednesday's practice due to a foot injury, Chris Easterling of the Akron Beacon Journal reports.
story: The rookie second-round pick is making his first career appearance on the injury report, but his ability to practice on at least a limited basis to begin Week 6 prep is a good sign for his chances of playing Sunday against the Ravens. The current betting favorite for the Offensive Rookie of the Year Award, Boston has opened his career with a 16-330-3 receiving line on 29 targets through five games.

headline: Boston caught three of seven targets for 46 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 17-12 loss to the Jets.
story: Boston's 29-yard touchdown catch with 6:15 left in the fourth quarter gave the Browns a 12-10 lead, but Cleveland failed to hold that advantage. The rookie second-round pick has caught 16 of 29 targets for 330 yards and three touchdowns while exceeding 40 receiving yards in each of his first five NFL outings. KC Concepcion, who was drafted 15 picks ahead of Boston at 24th overall, exited Sunday's loss due to a concussion. Boston could get a larger share of targets from Deshaun Watson if Concepcion doesn't rejoin Cleveland's WR room in Week 6 against the Ravens.

headline: Boston brought in four of seven targets for 89 yards in the Browns' 27-24 win over the Steelers on Thursday.
story: The impressive start to Boston's NFL career continued Thursday, with the rookie second-round pick leading the Browns in receiving yards and tying for runner-up status with Quinshon Judkins in targets. The bulk of Boston's production came on an impressive 60-yard reception to kick off an early second-quarter possession that culminated in a Judkins two-yard touchdown run. Boston has quickly amassed a 13-284-2 line on 22 targets through his first four career games, affording him plenty of momentum heading into a Week 5 road matchup against the Jets on Sunday, Oct. 11.

headline: Boston caught two of four targets for 41 yards during the Browns' 21-18 win over the Panthers on Sunday. He also caught a two-point conversion.
story: The rookie second-rounder was held without a catch until the fourth quarter, when he caught 28- and 13-yard passes from Deshaun Watson before the duo connected on a two-point conversion late in the fourth quarter to extend the Browns' lead to three points. Boston was unable to record a touchdown catch for a third-straight game, though he still finished Sunday's contest as the Browns' second-leading receiver behind tight end Harold Fannin (51). Boston, Fannin and rookie first-rounder KC Concepcion will continue to serve as Watson's top targets in the passing game, with Jerry Jeudy and Isaiah Bond working in rotation. Boston will take a 9-195-2 receiving line (on 15 targets) into Thursday's AFC North showdown against the Steelers.

headline: Boston caught five of seven targets for 95 yards and a touchdown in the Browns' 23-19 win over Tampa Bay on Sunday.
story: Boston's big play was a 55-yard touchdown late in the third quarter to pull the Browns even with the Bucs at 16-16. The rookie wideout caught a deep crosser and spun off several would-be tackles and dashed to the end zone. It was Boston's second long touchdown in as many weeks to begin his pro career. Through two games, the second-round pick has seven catches for 154 yards and two scores on 11 targets. He's shaping up as a boom-or-bust fantasy WR4 headed into next Sunday's home date with the Panthers.

headline: Boston caught two passes on four targets for 59 yards and a touchdown during the Browns' 34-10 loss to the Jaguars on Sunday.
story: It wasn't until the third play of the fourth quarter that Boston made his first NFL catch, a 13-yard pass from Deshaun Watson, before the duo connected on a 46-yard touchdown pass on the first play following the two-minute warning. Boston finished Sunday's game as the Browns' leader in receiving yards while fellow rookie KC Concepcion led the team in catches (four) and targets (five). There figures to be some growing pains for the Browns' offense this season given the amount of young talent. Cleveland will stay on the road for a Week 2 matchup against Tampa Bay on Sept. 20.

headline: Boston is listed as a starting wide receiver along with veteran Jerry Jeudy and 2026 first-round pick KC Concepcion on the Browns' unofficial depth chart.
story: The 39th overall pick in the 2026 Draft, Boston combined for one catch (on two targets) for 15 yards on 37 offensive snaps between his two appearances during the preseason. The output was nothing to write home about, but he appears set to be one of starting QB Deshaun Watson's key pass catchers to begin the campaign.

headline: Boston went without a target while playing 11 snaps on offense Saturday in the Browns' 31-7 preseason loss to the Bills.
story: After drawing two targets in the Browns' preseason opener a week earlier against the Bears and connecting with Deshaun Watson on a nifty 15-yard catch and run, Boston was held quiet in his limited snaps during the second exhibition game. Notably, Jerry Jeudy and KC Concepcion were both rested Saturday while Boston played, which suggests that the rookie second-round pick out of Washington currently sits no higher than third on the depth chart.

headline: Judkins (foot) didn't participate in Wednesday's practice, Chris Easterling of the Akron Beacon Journal reports.
story: Daniel Oyefusi of ESPN.com noted that Judkins was spotted Wednesday walking around the locker room without a walking boot on his right foot, but the running back ultimately wasn't able to mix into any drills during the Browns' first Week 6 practice session. Judkins will need to practice in some capacity Thursday or Friday for fantasy managers to feel good about his chances of suiting up Sunday against the Ravens. At least for the time being, Jaleel McLaughlin and Audric Estime are the healthy running backs on the Browns' active roster.

headline: Judkins was spotted Wednesday moving around the Cleveland locker room without a boot on his injured right ankle, Daniel Oyefusi of ESPN.com reports.
story: Per Oyefusi, Judkins isn't expected to practice Wednesday, but the fact that he's ditched his walking boot represents a tangible sign of progress in his recovery from the ankle injury he sustained in Sunday's loss to the Jets. Earlier in the week, head coach Todd Monken described Judkins as day-to-day, which suggests that the Browns haven't ruled out the possibility of their top running back playing this Sunday versus the Ravens. His activity -- or lack thereof -- in practices Thursday and Friday will likely guide the Browns' decision regarding whether or not he'll suit up this weekend.

headline: Browns head coach Todd Monken said that Judkins is considered day-to-day after sustaining a "tweak" to his ankle in Sunday's 17-12 loss to the Jets, and the running back hasn't been ruled out for a Week 6 game against the Ravens, Daniel Oyefusi of ESPN.com reports.
story: Though he was able to finish out Sunday's contest while accounting for 50 yards from scrimmage on 17 touches (14 carries, three receptions), Judkins handled a lower snap share (52.9 percent) than usual, likely due to the injury. The second-year back was spotted with a walking boot on his right foot following the game, but Monken's comments offer at least some optimism about Judkins' availability heading into Week 6. His practice participation Wednesday through Friday should help provide a clearer read on his status heading into next Sunday.

headline: Judkins was wearing a walking boot on his right foot after Sunday's 17-12 loss at the Jets, Chris Easterling of the Akron Beacon Journal reports.
story: It's unclear when Judkins may have suffered the injury, but he paced the Browns backfield in Week 5 with 14 carries for 44 yards while adding three catches (on four targets) for six yards. With reserve RB Raheim Sanders also exiting Sunday's game due to a hip issue, Jaleel McLaughlin is currently the only healthy RB on the active roster.

headline: Judkins rushed 17 times for 53 yards and a touchdown and brought in six of seven targets for 43 yards in the Browns' 27-24 win over the Steelers on Thursday.
story: Judkins was in his customary workhorse role in the Browns' ground attack, although as his final rushing line indicates, he found running room hard to come by on most of his carries. Even the second-year back's first rushing touchdown of the season didn't come easy, as Judkins had to power his way in from two yards out in the second quarter. However, he was able to find plenty of success as a receiver, finishing as the team leader in receptions and tying for runner-up status in targets with numbers that also qualified as new career-high figures. Judkins' backfield mates Raheim Sanders and Jaleel McLaughlin combined for just three carries between them -- although the latter took his one tote for a 28-yard touchdown -- so Cleveland's clear lead back will continue to helm the run game in a Week 5 road matchup against the Jets on Sunday, Oct. 11.

headline: Judkins rushed 18 times for 70 yards and brought in both targets for nine yards in the Browns' 21-18 win over the Panthers on Sunday.
story: Judkins took all but one of the Browns' running backs' carries, and he was able to capitalize on an injury-hampered Panthers defense to produce his best showing of the new season. He still finished under 4.0 yards per carry, but after averaging under 3.0 in each of the first two games, Sunday's effort was certainly an improvement. Judkins and the surprising 2-1 Browns now have a quick turnaround for a Week 4 home divisional clash against the Steelers on Thursday night.

headline: Judkins (personal) doesn't carry an injury designation for Sunday's game against Carolina, Scott Petrak of BrownsZone.com reports.
story: Judkins returned to full practice participation Friday after being limited Thursday due to a personal matter. He should be fine to handle his usual role as Cleveland's lead runner Sunday against the Panthers.

headline: Judkins (personal) was in uniform for the start of Friday's practice, Zac Jackson reports.
story: After being listed as a limited participant Thursday due to a personal matter, Judkins likely will return to full participation Friday. There's been no indication that he's in serious danger of missing Sunday's matchup with Carolina.

headline: Judkins (personal) was a limited participant at Thursday's practice, Daniel Oyefusi of ESPN.com reports.
story: It's unclear what personal matter kept Judkins from practicing without limitations Thursday, but Cleveland's starting running back isn't dealing with an injury. If Judkins can get back to full participation Friday, he'll likely avoid an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Panthers. Raheim Sanders and Jaleel McLaughlin are the healthy alternatives in Cleveland's backfield since Dylan Sampson (knee) is on IR.

headline: Judkins rushed 12 times for 21 yards and brought in all five targets for 27 yards in the Browns' 23-19 win over the Buccaneers on Sunday.
story: Judkins once again handled a clear No. 1 role in Cleveland's ground attack, but he unsurprisingly found running room at a premium against the Buccaneers' stout defensive front. The second-year back was able to make up for the lack of rushing production to an extent with his work as a receiver, which saw him tie for the second-most receptions on the afternoon for the Browns. Judkins is averaging a meager 2.3 yards per carry through the first two games, but he has a useful 7-44-0 receiving line on seven targets in that same span as a Week 3 home matchup against the Panthers approaches next Sunday.

headline: Judkins rushed 12 times for 33 yards and brought in both targets for 17 yards in the Browns' 34-10 loss to the Jaguars on Sunday.
story: Judkins operated as the unquestioned lead back for the Browns as expected, yet his opportunities on the ground were limited overall thanks to a game script that saw Cleveland already down 24-0 at the half. Judkins unsurprisingly found running room difficult to come by when he did carry the ball, but he was efficient with his pair of receptions. Judkins could face loaded defensive fronts most weeks if the Browns' quarterback play doesn't improve, and a Week 2 road matchup against the Buccaneers next Sunday doesn't offer much promise on paper.

headline: Judkins didn't play in Thursday's exhibition win over New England.
story: Judkins also missed the team's second preseason game due to an undisclosed injury, but he returned to practice this past Monday and seems to be past the issue. He ended up logging action in only the first of the Browns' exhibition contests, when he carried four times for nine yards. Judkins is the clear No. 1 RB for Cleveland and could be headed for a heavy workload on a team that may again deploy a shaky passing game.

headline: Judkins (undisclosed) took part in team drills at Tuesday's practice session, Daniel Oyefusi of ESPN.com reports.
story: Judkins got some work in at Monday's session after missing time last week with an unspecified minor injury, and he was able to work alongside the rest of the group a day later. As such, consider him back at full speed moving forward.

headline: Judkins (undisclosed) returned to practice Monday, Daniel Oyefusi of ESPN.com reports.
story: Judkins missed the final two practices of last week before sitting out Saturday's preseason loss to the Bills due to what coach Todd Monken described as "a little something nagging, nothing big," per Kelsey Russo of the Browns' official site. Even though he's mixing back into drills, Judkins may be eased in with Week 1 still roughly three weeks on the horizon.

headline: Judkins (undisclosed) is not expected to play in Saturday's preseason game against the Bills, Kelsey Russo of the Browns' official site reports.
story: Judkins missed consecutive training camp practices earlier this week while recovering from an undisclosed issue. It looks like he'll observe Saturday's exhibition game in street clothes, and it's unclear whether he'll suit up for the Browns' preseason finale against the Patriots on Thursday. Judkins' absence means Dylan Sampson will lead the Browns' backfield against the Bills, with Raheim Sanders, Ahmani Marshall and Davon Booth also in the mix for reps.

headline: Judkins (undisclosed) didn't practice Thursday, but coach Todd Monken said afterward that the running back is tending to "a little something nagging, nothing big," Kelsey Russo of the Browns' official site reports.
story: Judkins has missed back-to-back sessions due to an unspecified injury, but considering Monken's comment, the Browns nonetheless are taking a cautious approach with the second-year pro. As a rookie second-round pick in 2025, Judkins tallied 230 carries for 827 yards and seven touchdowns while hauling in 26 of 36 targets for 171 yards in 14 regular-season games before suffering a dislocated right ankle and broken right fibula Week 16 that required surgery. He was taking 11-on-11 drills as of mid-May and otherwise was back to 100 percent before the recent setback, health-wise. It's unclear if Judkins will suit up for Saturday's preseason contest against the Bills as a result.

headline: Judkins (undisclosed) wasn't spotted at practice Thursday, Daniel Oyefusi of ESPN.com reports.
story: Judkins has been absent for back-to-back practices due to an unspecified issue that coach Todd Monken describes as a "nagging injury" per Scott Petrak of the Elyria Chronicle-Telegram. His status for Saturday's preseason tilt against the Bills has yet to be determined at this point. Judkins is locked in as Cleveland's top backfield option on early downs, though fellow second-year pro Dylan Sampson figures to get some opportunities in passing situations.

headline: Judkins wasn't present at practice Wednesday due to an undisclosed minor injury, Mary Kay Cabot of The Cleveland Plain Dealer reports.
story: Judkins' absence may have stemmed from Tuesday's session, when he was front and center to some unnecessary hits, per Cabot. The Browns are hosting a joint practice with the Bills on Thursday before taking on Buffalo in preseason action Saturday, but it's unclear if Judkins will suit up for either of those. Dylan Sampson would stand to benefit with more work for as long as Judkins is sidelined.

headline: Judkins carried the ball four times for nine yards in Saturday's 34-10 preseason loss to the Bears.
story: The second-year back got the start for the Browns but played only the first quarter before calling it a day. Judkins is the clear top dog in the backfield, and after gaining 998 scrimmage yards on 256 touches over 14 regular-season games as a rookie, the 2025 second-round pick is expected to take on a larger workload in 2026 under new head coach Todd Monken.

headline: The Browns signed Estime to the 53-man roster Tuesday.
story: Estime signed to the Vikings practice squad in late September before signing with Cleveland. The 23-year-old will be behind Jaleel McLaughlin on the depth chart, who is the only other healthy running back on the Browns' roster. Dylan Sampson (knee) remains on injured reserve, and Quinshon Judkins (foot) and Raheim Sanders (hip) are both dealing with injuries after Sunday's 17-12 loss to the Jets.

headline: The Browns are expected to sign Estime off the Vikings' practice squad to the active roster, NFL reporter Jordan Schultz relays.
story: The Browns are in need of backfield depth, given that Dylan Sampson (knee) is on injured reserve and that both Quinshon Judkins (foot) and Raheim Sanders (hip) sustained their respective injuries during Sunday's 17-12 loss to the Jets. Jaleel McLaughlin is currently the only healthy running back on the Browns' roster, so Estime could have a sizable role in Week 6 against the Ravens on Sunday depending on the practice participation of Judkins, Sanders and Sampson over the coming days.

headline: The Vikings signed Estime to the practice squad Wednesday.
story: Estime worked out for the team Tuesday and will provide backfield depth behind Aaron Jones, Demond Claiborne and special-teamer DeeJay Dallas while Jordan Mason (thumb) remains on injured reserve for at least the next two games. Estime has handled 122 career regular-season carries for 508 yards and three touchdowns.

headline: The Vikings hosted Estime (thigh) for a workout Tuesday, Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston reports.
story: The Saints waived Estime from injured reserve with an injury settlement last Tuesday. The running back suffered a thigh injury in early September and was quickly placed on IR, only to be waived shortly after. Estime played in seven games for New Orleans during the 2025 regular season, rushing 46 times for 198 yards and a touchdown.

headline: The Saints waived Estime (thigh) from injured reserve Tuesday with an injury settlement, Katherine Terrell of ESPN.com reports.
story: Estime was placed on injured reserve Sept. 12 due to a thigh injury. The running back was set to return to the team as a depth option after a short stint on IR. However, with Alvin Kamara making his season debut in Week 2 and Kendre Miller and CJ Donaldson also on hand behind Travis Etienne, Estime was deemed expendable. Estime is now a free agent and can sign with any team as soon as he recovers from his thigh injury.

headline: The Saints placed Estime (thigh) on injured reserve Saturday, Ross Jackson of WWL Louisiana reports.
story: Estime was ruled out for Sunday's game against Detroit with a thigh injury. The running back's injury came out of nowhere but movement to IR likely means it is a significant issue. Estime will need to miss the first four games of the regular season before he is eligible to return to the field.

headline: Estime (thigh) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Lions.
story: It's unclear when Estime suffered the thigh injury, but he didn't practice at all this week after leading the Saints in rushing in the preseason finale two weeks ago. If Alvin Kamara (knee) is unable to go against Detroit, Kendre Miller would serve as the RB2 behind Travis Etienne.

headline: Estime (thigh) did not participate at practice Thursday.
story: The thigh injury that landed Estime on the Saints' official injury report Wednesday kept him sidelined Thursday. He'll probably need to practice in some form Friday to have a realistic chance of playing Sunday at Detroit.

headline: Estime (thigh) did not participate in Wednesday's practice.
story: Estime is dealing with a thigh issue that kept him out of the first official practice of Week 1. The running back will need to upgrade his participation to at least limited by Friday's session to have a shot at playing in Sunday's contest against the Lions.

headline: Estime is listed as the fourth running back on the Saints' 53-man roster, Grant Chachere of SI.com reports.
story: Estime was able to beat out Zamir White and Devin Neal (hamstring) for that final backfield depth spot on the active roster for the regular season. Estime has worked in a rotational role in his first two years in the NFL, but the 2024 fifth-rounder would operate in a larger role behind Travis Etienne in Week 1 against the Lions if one or both of Alvin Kamara (knee) and Kendre Miller (undisclosed) were to be limited or ruled out.

headline: Estime rushed four times for 46 yards and caught all three of his targets for 22 yards in Friday's 27-24 preseason win over the Cowboys.
story: Estime led the Saints in rushing Friday, finishing with four more yards than Kendre Miller thanks to a 33-yard run. Injuries to Alvin Kamara (knee) and Devin Neal (hamstring) could open the door for Estime to make the 53-man roster, though Miller and recent trade acquisition Zamir White are also competing for spots in New Orleans' backfield behind Travis Etienne.

headline: Estime (ankle) participated in practice Monday, Ross Jackson of WWL Louisiana reports.
story: Estime had missed some time due to an ankle injury, but the running back's return to Monday's walkthrough session will enable him to re-enter the depth equation in a New Orleans backfield that's dealing with several injuries. In seven regular-season games with the Saints last season, Estime carried 46 times for 198 yards and one touchdown, adding 12 catches for 102 yards.

headline: Estime is expected to miss some time with his ankle injury, Ross Jackson of WWL Louisiana reports.
story: While Estime has avoided a serious injury, he's going to be down for a little bit, per Jackson. It's a bad break for Estime, who is trying to win a job in the Saints' backfield that just lost Alvin Kamara (knee) to a sprained MCL. Estime is competing with the likes of Kendre Miller and Devin Neal behind Travis Etienne. Across seven regular-season appearances last season, Estime rushed 46 times for 198 yards and one touchdown.

headline: Estime suffered an ankle injury during Saturday's preseason loss to the Jaguars, Mike Triplett of NewOrleans.Football reports.
story: Estime was injured on a hard hit after reeling in a catch for a six-yard loss in the second quarter. Prior to that, the 22-year-old had been impressive, breaking multiple tackles for a nine-yard TD run on New Orleans' first offensive play and tallying 28 yards on five total carries. Estime has a chance to earn the No. 3 RB role for the Saints, but he'll likely need to get healthy enough to show what he has to offer in additional preseason contests.

headline: Estime went to the locker room due to an apparent leg injury during Saturday's preseason game against Jacksonville, John Hendrix of AthlonSports.com reports.
story: Estime was hurt when he was hit hard on a catch that went for a six-yard loss. The third-year tailback went to the injury tent and then tested things out on the sideline before heading into the locker room. It remains to be seen if Estime is dealing with anything serious, but he was having a good game prior to exiting, rushing five times for 28 yards and a touchdown. He's in the running to be the Saints' No. 3 RB behind Travis Etienne and Alvin Kamara.

headline: The Browns placed Sanders (hip) on injured reserve Tuesday.
story: Sanders opened the year as Cleveland's No. 3 running back but saw his role increase after Dylan Sampson (knee) landed on IR. During the season's first four games, Sanders gained 42 yards on eight carries and added eight catches for 49 yards on nine targets before going down with a hip injury in Week 5. Sanders will be sidelined for at least the next four games.

headline: Sanders (hip) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Jets.
story: Sanders exited the game in the fourth quarter with a hip injury. The running back rushed three times for 12 yards and caught his sole target for one yard before exiting the contest.

headline: Sanders accrued two rushes for nine yards and gathered in both of his two targets for seven yards during Thursday's 27-24 win versus the Steelers.
story: Sanders logged 22 offensive snaps, his second-highest mark of the 2026 campaign. However, the 24-year-old was a non-factor offensively. Instead, it was Jaleel McLaughlin who took advantage of his limited workload by scoring a 28-yard rushing touchdown early in the second quarter. While Sanders should remain the No. 2 back on the depth chart behind Quinshon Judkins, assuming the latter stays healthy, he will be difficult to trust from a fantasy standpoint moving ahead.

headline: Sanders caught his sole target for seven yards, had two rushes for four yards and returned two kickoffs for 50 yards in Sunday's 23-19 win over the Buccaneers.
story: Sanders played 11 offensive snaps and six special-teams snaps in Sunday's contest. Despite the small snap share, Sanders found plenty to do in Cleveland's first win of the season, making key plays for both the offensive and special-teams units.

headline: Sanders will have the opportunity to work in an expanded role in the Browns' offense after Dylan Sampson (knee) was placed on injured reserve Tuesday, Scott Petrak of BrownsZone reports.
story: Sampson injured his knee on a kickoff return during Sunday's 34-10 loss to the Jaguars, and he'll be required to miss at least the next four games while on IR. Sanders finished that game with three catches on as many targets for 25 yards along with a one-yard carry, but moving forward, he should see more offensive snaps as the Browns' RB2 behind Quinshon Judkins, with Jaleel McLaughlin slotting in as the No. 3 backfield option. The Browns will stay on the road for a Week 2 tilt against the Buccaneers, whose defense gave up 106 rushing yards and one touchdown on 27 carries (3.9 YPC) in a 33-27 loss to the Bengals in Week 1.

headline: Sanders caught all three of his targets for 25 yards and added one carry for one yard in Sunday's 34-10 loss to the Jaguars. He also returned three kickoffs for 130 yards.
story: Sanders had an opportunity to mix into the offense after Dylan Sampson (knee) sustained an injury during the Week 1 contest. Sanders played 18 of the 51 offensive snaps for the Browns while also making an impact with his trio of kickoff returns. Quinshon Judkins remains the unquestioned leader of the Browns' ground attack, but Sanders would be in line to serve as his primary backup in a Week 2 road matchup against the Buccaneers if Sampson remains sidelined.

headline: Wallace (knee) has been ruled out ahead of Sunday's game against the Jets, Daniel Oyefusi of ESPN.com reports.
story: Wallace has not practiced since sustaining a knee injury in the Browns' Week 3 win over the Panthers. The wide receiver will now miss consecutive games due to the issue, again leaving Malachi Corley as the No. 5 wideout option for the Browns' offense.

headline: Wallace (knee) didn't practice Thursday.
story: Wallace hurt his knee in Week 3 against Carolina and didn't play last Thursday in a win over the Steelers. He hasn't practiced since getting injured, so his chances of suiting up Sunday aren't promising. Wallace has yet to log a target this season, but another absence will likely mean that Malachi Corley gets more opportunities on offense.

headline: Wallace (knee) did not participate at practice Wednesday.
story: Wallace sat out Cleveland's contest versus the Steelers in Week 4 due to a knee injury, and now his availability for Week 5 is up in the air, too. He'll probably need to return to practice in some capacity Thursday or Friday to have a realistic chance of playing Sunday against the Jets.

headline: Wallace (knee) has been ruled out for Thursday's game against the Steelers.
story: A knee injury prevented Wallace from practicing all week, so the sixth-year pro will observe Thursday's game from the sidelines, which means Isaiah Bond and Malachi Corley are both in line to see a slight uptick in offensive snaps. Wallace's next opportunity to play is Week 5 against the Jets on Sunday, Oct. 11.

headline: Wallace (knee) didn't participate in Cleveland's practice Tuesday, Daniel Oyefusi of ESPN.com reports.
story: Wallace is in danger of missing Thursday's matchup versus the Steelers, as he was also listed as a non-participant in Monday's practice estimate after suffering a knee injury during the Week 3 win over Carolina. Isaiah Bond and Malachi Corley could be in line for increased playing time if Wallace is unable to suit up for Thursday's game.

headline: Wallace (knee) did not participate in the Browns' estimated practice Monday, Adam Caplan of SiriusXM NFL Radio reports.
story: Wallace stayed down on the field after a kickoff return during the Browns' 21-18 win over the Panthers on Sunday, Daniel Oyefusi of ESPN.com reports. The wide receiver's injury wasn't announced until Monday, so the knee issue may be minor. If Wallace cannot suit up for Tuesday's practice session in at least a limited capacity, his chances of playing in Thursday night's game against the Steelers will likely be in jeopardy.

headline: Ryan (calf) has been ruled out ahead of Sunday's game against the Jets, Daniel Oyefusi of ESPN.com reports.
story: Ryan popped up on Thursday's injury report with a calf injury and could practice only in a limited capacity. The tight end downgraded to a DNP in Friday's session, forcing the Browns to rule him out of Sunday's game against the Jets.

headline: Ryan logged a limited practice Thursday due to a calf injury.
story: Carsen wasn't listed on the injury report Wednesday, so he likely picked up the calf issue during practice. The rookie has seen most of his action on special teams this season, logging only two snaps so far on offense. As such, if Ryan is unable to play Sunday against the Jets, it probably won't affect Cleveland's passing game much.

headline: Ryan (foot) caught both of his targets for nine yards in Thursday's 37-13 preseason win over the Patriots.
story: Ryan managed to suit up two days after exiting Tuesday's practice early due to a foot injury. The rookie seventh-round pick is aiming to secure a spot on Cleveland's 53-man roster in a TE room led by Harold Fannin.

headline: Ryan (foot) exited Tuesday's practice to talk with trainers, Mary Kay Cabot of The Cleveland Plain Dealer reports.
story: The tight end walked to the fieldhouse with a trainer after being checked for a foot injury on the sideline. The advanced analysis could just be for safety, but it looks like Ryan has sustained a potentially problematic foot issue. If the rookie seventh-rounder must miss time, Jack Stoll and Dae'Quan Wright will likely see more opportunities to prove they are 53-man roster material in Saturday's preseason game against the Bills.

headline: Hall (ankle) has been ruled out ahead of Sunday's game against the Jets, Daniel Oyefusi of ESPN.com reports.
story: Hall has not been able to practice since sustaining an ankle injury in the Browns' Week 4 win over the Steelers last Thursday. The defensive tackle's absence is compounded by the absence of Mason Graham (knee/ankle), leaving the team with no reserve options on the 53-man roster behind Maliek Collins and Adin Huntington.

headline: Hall (ankle) didn't practice Wednesday or Thursday.
story: Hall suffered an ankle injury in last Thursday's win over Pittsburgh. Though he was able to return to that contest, the third-year defensive tackle has been held out of practice for the first two days of Week 5 prep, giving him a gloomy outlook for Sunday's matchup against the Jets. Mason Graham (knee) is also unlikely to suit up Sunday, so Cleveland could rely on Maliek Collins and Adin Huntington to hold down the fort.

headline: Hall (ankle) has returned to action Thursday night versus the Steelers, Chris Easterling of the Akron Beacon Journal reports.
story: Hall was sidelined to open the second half after suffering an ankle injury in the second quarter. The 23-year-old is now back out on the field, manning a prominent role on Cleveland's defensive line.

headline: Hall (ankle) is questionable to return to Thursday night's matchup with Pittsburgh.
story: Hall suffered an ankle injury in the second quarter when his teammate Jared Verse rolled up on his lower leg. The defensive lineman's status for the rest of the game is now uncertain. With Mason Graham (knee) already done for the night, Maliek Collins and Adin Huntington will operate as the team's primary options at defensive tackle.

headline: Hall (undisclosed) was a full participant in Tuesday's practice, Zac Jackson of The Athletic reports.
story: Hall was expected to return to practice sometime this week, so Tuesday's participation is no shock. The defensive tackle missed last Saturday's preseason opener against the Bears due to an unknown issue but should be set to play a few snaps in next Saturday's contest against the Bills. Hall's return to the lineup means Sam Kamara and Adin Huntington will likely see fewer reps in Saturday's contest.

headline: Hall (undisclosed) did not participate in Saturday's preseason opener against the Bears, Mary Cay Cabot of cleveland.com reports.
story: Hall is expected to return to practice this week after missing some time with an undisclosed injury. The defensive tackle's return should bolster the Browns' defensive line depth as they look toward Saturday's preseason game against the Bills. If practice goes well for Hall, he should start opposite Mason Graham on the interior defensive line in Saturday's contest.

headline: Jenkins (back) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Jets, Daniel Oyefusi of ESPN.com reports.
story: Jenkins will end up missing each of the Browns' first five games of the regular season due to a back injury, which prevented him from practicing all week. His next chance to make his 2026 regular-season debut is Week 6 against the Ravens on Sunday, Oct. 18.

headline: Jenkins (back) is officially listed as out for Thursday's game versus Pittsburgh.
story: Jenkins was able to return to practice during the week on a limited basis, but he'll have to wait at least one more game to make his 2026 regular-season debut. Rookie third-rounder Austin Barber should get another start at right guard in Week 4.

headline: Jenkins (back) is listed as out for Sunday's game against the Panthers, Zac Jackson of The Athletic reports.
story: Jenkins continues to battle a back injury, and considering he hasn't been practicing, it's unknown when he will be ready to go. While Jenkins is out of commission, Austin Barber remains in line to start.

headline: Jenkins (back) is out for Sunday's game against the Buccaneers, Kelsey Russo of the Browns' official site reports.
story: Jenkins was also unable to suit up in Week 1 due to his lingering back injury, and now he'll have to wait at least one more week before making his season debut. Rookie third-rounder Austin Barber should again start at right guard in Jenkins' place in Week 2.

headline: Jenkins (back) did not participate in practice Thursday, Scott Petrak of the Elyria Chronicle-Telegram reports.
story: The offensive guard was not able to play in Week 1 due to the back issue. At the moment, he's not on track to play in Week 2, either. Austin Barber has been his replacement at right guard.

headline: Jenkins (back) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Jaguars.
story: With Jenkins out for the Week 1 opener, third-round rookie Austin Barber is expected to make the start at left guard for Cleveland. Jenkins appeared in all 17 regular-season games last season, making four starts.

headline: Jenkins (back) did not participate at the Browns' practice Thursday, Daniel Oyefusi of ESPN.com reports.
story: Jenkins left Wednesday's practice early with a back injury, and he was unable to give it a go a day later. If he can't play Sunday against the Jaguars, Austin Barber is the most likely candidate to start at right guard in the team's regular-season opener.

headline: Jeudy hauled in three of seven targets for 19 yards during Sunday's 17-12 loss against the Jets.
story: Quarterback Deshaun Watson struggled mightily against a tough Jets defense in Week 5, completing just 15 of his 33 pass attempts for 155 yards and getting sacked eight times. Jeudy's production still managed to lag behind even that baseline, as he averaged fewer than three yards per target Sunday. He'll be hoping to at least keep up the target volume in a Week 6 matchup versus the Ravens.

headline: Jeudy caught all three of his targets for 36 yards in Thursday's 27-24 win over Pittsburgh.
story: It looked like Jeudy could be shut out for the third straight game after finishing the first half with no targets. However, the veteran wideout gave Cleveland a first down with a nine-yard reception late in the third quarter, then came up with two big catches -- a 17-yarder and a 10-yarder -- after the two-minute warning in the fourth to help set up Andre Szmyt's game-winning field goal. The two fourth-quarter catches alone accounted for more yardage than Jeudy had recorded across his first three games of the campaign, so perhaps he and QB Deshaun Watson have found some chemistry that they can carry over into a Week 5 matchup versus the Jets.

headline: Jeudy finished Sunday's 21-18 victory against Carolina with no targets or touches.
story: It was the second straight week that Jeudy didn't log a reception, and this time he didn't even get a target (he logged just one in Week 2 versus Tampa Bay). The veteran wideout continues to be on the field fairly often -- he's recorded an offensive snap share of over 50 percent in each of the Browns' three contests, including Sunday when he played 51 percent. However, he doesn't seem to be clicking well with QB Deshaun Watson, and at this point fantasy managers have little reason to include him in their lineups.

headline: Jeudy failed to haul in his lone target during the Browns' 23-19 win over the Buccaneers on Sunday.
story: Jeudy couldn't improve on his 2-26-0 line (on four targets) during the Browns' Week 1 loss to the Jaguars. The seventh-year pro played 34 of 58 offensive snaps Sunday (58.6 percent), which was third most among Cleveland wide receivers behind rookies Denzel Boston (54) and KC Concepcion (38). Jeudy finished the 2025 regular season with the second-most receiving yards on the Browns, but it appears Boston, Concepcion, tight end Harold Fannin and even running back Quinshon Judkins are the preferred targets for Deshaun Watson to open the season. Jeudy will look for better results in Cleveland's home opener against Carolina on Sept. 27.

headline: Jeudy caught two passes (on four targets) for 26 yards during the Browns' 34-10 loss to the Jaguars on Sunday.
story: Jeudy's first target from Deshaun Watson in the first quarter resulted in an interception, leading to a 30-yard touchdown pass from Trevor Lawrence to Parker Washington. Jeudy and Watson connected on passes of 20 and six yards late in the second quarter, but the seventh-year wide receiver did not see a target in the second half. His 32 snaps on offense were third most behind rookies Denzel Boston (47) and KC Concepcion (35), and Jeudy also is competing with tight end Harold Fannin for targets. Up next is a Week 2 road clash against the Buccaneers on Sept. 20.

headline: Jeudy is listed as a starting wide receiver on Cleveland's initial depth chart ahead of the team's Week 1 game against the Jaguars.
story: It comes as no surprise after the Browns cut Cedric Tillman at the end of training camp. Jeudy is listed as a starter alongside rookie wideouts KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston. Jeudy displayed no chemistry with Shedeur Sanders last season, as the veteran wideout finished 2025 with just 50 catches for 602 yards and two touchdowns on 106 targets. His 47.2 percent catch rate was fifth worst out of 197 qualified pass catchers, and of the 38 players in the NFL to see at least 100 targets, Jeudy's 602 yards were just two more than Jake Ferguson at the bottom of the list. Concepcion is expected to become the go-to target in Cleveland, with Boston operating as the big-bodied X receiver. Jeudy will face far more competition for targets.

headline: Jeudy will not play in the Browns' preseason game against the Bills on Saturday, Daniel Oyefusi of ESPN.com reports.
story: Jeudy played in the Browns' preseason opener against the Bears this past Saturday, when he caught both of his targets for 18 yards in a 34-10 loss. Jeudy, KC Concepcion and Cedric Tillman (undisclosed) will be sidelined against Buffalo, so Denzel Boston will lead the Browns' wide receiver corps, with Isaiah Bond, Tylan Wallace and Malachi Corley also in line for additional reps.

headline: Green (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Jets, though he will serve as the Browns' emergency quarterback.
story: Green will be inactive for the fifth consecutive contest but is listed as the Browns' QB3, meaning he will take over if Deshaun Watson and Shedeur Sanders exit the game due to injury, illness or ejection.

headline: Green (coach's decision) is inactive for Thursday's game against the Steelers, though he will serve as the Browns' emergency quarterback.
story: Green will be inactive for the fourth consecutive game but is listed as Cleveland's QB3. That means Green won't be on the field unless Deshaun Watson and Shedeur Sanders exit the contest due to injury, illness or ejection.

headline: Green (coach's decision) is inactive but serving as the emergency third quarterback against the Panthers on Sunday, Kelsey Russo of the Browns' official site reports.
story: Because he's serving as the emergency QB3, the rookie sixth-rounder is prohibited from taking the field Sunday unless both starter Deshaun Watson and backup Shedeur Sanders were to leave the game due to injury, illness or ejection.

headline: Green (coach's decision) is inactive as the emergency third quarterback for Sunday's game against the Buccaneers.
story: Green will once again serve as the third option behind Deshaun Watson and Shedeur Sanders. The quarterback can only enter the game if both players ahead of him cannot continue to play in Sunday's game due to injury, illness or ejection. The sixth-round rookie is likely set to fill this role for the remainder of the season unless either Watson or Sanders misses time.

headline: Green (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's matchup with the Jaguars.
story: The rookie is serving as the emergency third option behind Deshaun Watson and Shedeur Sanders, which means he can only enter the contest if the first two quarterbacks are injured, sick or otherwise unavailable. Green was selected in the sixth round of the draft out of Arkansas.
