headline: Gibbs carried the ball 29 times for 156 yards and two touchdowns and caught all five of his targets for 30 yards in Sunday's 31-30 overtime win over the Saints.
story: He did lose a fumble, but there wasn't much to criticize about Gibbs' performance otherwise. The star running back opened the scoring with a one-yard plunge in the first quarter, then added another one-yard TD on the Lions' first possession of the second half. Gibbs set a career high with 320 touches in 2025 (243 carries and 77 catches), but he could be headed for even bigger volume this season with David Montgomery no longer in Detroit to siphon away reps. Gibbs will look to keep rolling in Week 2 on the road against the Bills.

headline: Gibbs had a strong day in the Lions' final practice of training camp Thursday, most notably running for 59- and 16-yard touchdowns during the session, Tim Twentyman of the team's official site reports.
story: After being contained on the first two of the first-team offense's eight drives on the day, Gibbs delivered his biggest gain of the day on the Lions' third possession. On the second play of that drive, Gibbs followed a block from right guard Tate Ratledge, then found daylight while bouncing out to the outside and raced past cornerback Avonte Maddox for a 59-yard house call. He then finished practice with his second touchdown of the day, taking a fourth-and-1 pitch to the outside and following a Penei Sewell block to beat multiple defenders to the pylon. The two scoring jaunts were demonstrative of Gibbs' trademark explosiveness in open space, but now that David Montgomery is in Houston, the Lions are likely to turn to Gibbs to add more work to his plate in the form of increased usage in goal-line situations and as a runner on early downs. Detroit signed Isiah Pacheco this offseason with the goal of having him take on some of those functions that Montgomery had handled, but Pacheco won't be available until Week 5 at the earliest while he recovers from a back injury as well as an MCL sprain.

headline: Williams (foot) is active for Sunday's game against the Cardinals.
story: Williams was spotted wearing a walking boot and didn't practice Wednesday. He logged limited practice sessions Thursday and Friday but still couldn't avoid a questionable designation. However, Williams has since been cleared for action after amassing a season-high six total tackles in the 32-26 loss to Carolina in Week 4.

headline: Meeks (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against Arizona.
story: Meeks appeared in the Lions' first four games of the 2026 campaign but will be a healthy scratch in Week 5. The 23-year-old hasn't had a productive season, catching his only target for eight yards.

headline: Mays (wrist) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Cardinals.
story: Mays' 21-day window to return from injured reserve opened Wednesday, and he was a limited practice participant all week. He's not quite ready to return, but with the Lions on a bye for Week 6, Mays' next chance to play is Week 7 against Green Bay on Sunday, Oct. 25.

headline: The Lions designated Mays (wrist) for return from injured reserve Wednesday, Richard Silva of The Detroit News reports.
story: The move opens a 21-day window during which Mays can be officially activated from IR before he'd have to stay there for the rest of the campaign. Once he has fully recovered from the wrist fracture he sustained during the preseason, he projects to take over the starting center job from free-agent acquisition Juice Scruggs.

headline: Mays (wrist) is targeting a Week 7 return from injured reserve, Dave Birkett of the Detroit Free Press reports.
story: Mays was placed on IR on Aug. 30. The center fractured his wrist in the preseason but is set to return to the active roster soon. If Mays can get back in action after the Lions' Week 6 bye, he should be able to reclaim the starting center role from Juice Scruggs to boost the team's interior offensive line.

headline: Mays (wrist) is looking to return from injured reserve by mid-October, Dave Birkett of the Detroit Free Press reports.
story: Mays was placed on IR during the Aug. 30 cutdown day. The center fractured his wrist during the preseason, but is eyeing a quick month and a half of downtime before being able to return to protecting Jared Goff. While Mays remains on IR, Juice Scruggs will be the starting safety for the Lions.

headline: Mays (wrist) was placed on injured reserve on Sunday by the Lions with a designation to return, Tom Pelissero of Netflix reports.
story: Mays suffered a fractured wrist in early August, and he will now be forced to miss at least four contests to open the regular season. The 27-year-old is expected to operate as the team's starting center this season, and in his absence, Seth McLaughlin will get a chance to handle that role.

headline: Mays (wrist) was placed on injured reserve by the Lions on Sunday with a designation to return, Tom Pelissero of Netflix reports.
story: Mays suffered a fractured wrist during the preseason, and he will now be forced to miss at least four games to open the regular season. The 27-year-old was expected to operate as the team's starting center this year, so in his absence, Seth McLaughlin will get a chance to handle that role to open 2026.

headline: Branch (Achilles) has been ruled out ahead of Sunday's game against the Cardinals.
story: Branch returned to practice Wednesday after the Lions opened up his 21-day practice window. The strong safety managed to log limited practice in all three Week 5 prep sessions but is not quite ready to return to the field. Christian Izien will continue to start at strong safety while Branch puts the finishing touches on his recovery.

headline: Branch (Achilles) had his 21-day practice window opened by the Lions on Sunday, Richard Silva of The Detroit News reports.
story: Branch was limited in Wednesday's practice, but it was an encouraging sign to see the fourth-year pro back on the field following a lengthy recovery from a torn Achilles that he sustained in early December of 2025. The Lions' secondary has been one of the worst in the league this season, and while Branch's return would be a significant upgrade to the unit, he'll likely need to log multiple full practices before being activated from the reserve/PUP list. While it's unlikely he'd play, Branch's first opportunity to make his 2026 debut is Sunday against the Cardinals.

headline: Head coach Dan Campbell said Friday that Branch (Achilles) is close to returning, Tim Twentyman of the Lions' official site reports.
story: "Close" is a relative term, so it's unclear how close Branch actually is, considering he remains on the reserve/PUP list and has yet to begin practicing. It sounds like that could change next week. The Lions have been relying on Roger McCreary at slot cornerback in Branch's absence.

headline: The Lions placed Branch (Achilles) on the reserve/PUP list Sunday, Tom Pelissero of Netflix reports.
story: Branch spent the entirety of training camp on the active/PUP list, enabling the safety to be placed on the reserve list to begin the regular season. The 24-year-old will now be required to miss the first four weeks of the season at least before he can return to the Lions' active roster. With fellow safety Kerby Joseph (knee) also on the reserve/PUP list, the tandem of Avonte Maddox and Chuck Clark will likely start the season in the Lions' secondary.

headline: Izien recorded 11 tackles (seven solo) including 1.0 sacks during Sunday's 32-26 loss at Carolina.
story: Izien recorded the first sack of his career when he brought down quarterback Bryce Young for a loss of one early in the fourth quarter Sunday, and he totaled 11 tackles for the second straight game. His recent production should have put him on the IDP radar in most formats going into a Week 5 matchup at Arizona.

headline: Izien posted 11 tackles (nine solo) and one defensed pass Sunday in a 31-24 win over the Jets.
story: Izien paced the Lions in stops while playing all but two of the team's defensive snaps. The 26-year-old appears to be fully recovered from the groin injury that caused him to sit out Detroit's season opener. Izien has taken on a starting safety role due to Brian Branch (Achilles) and Kerby Joseph (knee) both being on the PUP list.

headline: Izien (groin) was considered to be a full participant at the Lions' walkthrough practice Monday.
story: Izien was unavailable for the team's 31-30 overtime win against New Orleans on Sunday as a result of a groin issue, but he now appears to be on track to make his season debut in Week 2. The 26-year-old is expected to operate as a top reserve option behind Roger McCreary at slot cornerback, and his first test of the season will come Thursday night against the Bills.

headline: Izien (groin) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Saints.
story: The safety logged limited practice sessions in the week leading up to the game and entered the weekend with a questionable tag. With Brian Branch (Achilles) and Kerby Joseph (knee) also unavailable for Sunday, the Lions will have to roll with Avonte Maddox, Chuck Clark and Thomas Harper as their safeties and Roger McCreary as their slot corner.

headline: Izien (groin) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Saints.
story: Izien has dealt with a groin injury throughout Week 1, logging limited participation in three consecutive practices. It is unclear how much the issue inhibits the reserve defensive back. If Izien must miss Sunday's contest, the Lions will likely elevate a defensive back from the practice squad to the active roster to fill in, as both Brian Branch (Achilles) and Kerby Joseph (knee) will miss the contest.

headline: Campbell recorded 14 tackles (six solo) during Sunday's 32-26 loss at Carolina.
story: Campbell was on the field for all 75 of the Lions' defensive snaps in Week 4, and he managed his highest tackle total of the season so far. He profiles as a high-floor IDP option in most formats heading into a Week 5 tilt at Arizona.

headline: Campbell made six tackles (two solo) in the Lions' 41-31 loss to the Bills on Thursday night.
story: Campbell played all 74 defensive snaps for the Lions, displaying intense physical conditioning against a Bills offense that was constantly on the field. The starting middle linebacker posted a similar stat line during Week 1 in a long game against the Saints, showing consistent availability and production for the team's defense.

headline: Campbell posted seven tackles (five solo) during the Lions' 31-30 overtime win over the Saints on Sunday.
story: Campbell was the only Lions player to play all 90 defensive snaps during Sunday's OT win, and he finished tied for the second-most tackles on the team behind D.J. Reed (10, foot). Campbell entered 2026 on the heels of a career year in 2025, when he tallied 176 tackles (89 solo), including 5.0 sacks, four pass defenses, three forced fumbles and two fumble recoveries across 17 regular-season games. The fourth-year linebacker inked a four-year, $81 million contract extension with the Lions in May, ensuring that the Iowa product will be a key piece to defense for years to come.

headline: Conklin (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Jets.
story: Conklin has been used sparingly through the first two games of the regular season, and the veteran tight end will be a healthy scratch Sunday against the team he played for from 2022 to 2024. Brock Wright and Jackson Meeks will provide depth at the position behind Sam LaPorta, and Conklin's next opportunity to play is Week 4 against the Panthers on Sunday, Oct. 4.

headline: The Lions signed Conklin on Tuesday.
story: Conklin failed to make the 53-man roster over the weekend but is quickly back with the team in a series of moves. The 31-year-old Conklin caught seven passes for 101 scoreless yards across 13 regular-season games with the Chargers last season and will serve as depth behind Sam LaPorta and Brock Wright with the Lions.

headline: Reed (ribs) is active for Sunday night's matchup with the Panthers.
story: Reed will ultimately be able to give it a go after operating as a limited participant a practice throughout the week with a rib injury that he suffered in Week 3. The cornerback will likely be tasked with trying to hold Tetairoa McMillan in check during Sunday Night Football.

headline: Reed (ribs) is listed as questionable ahead of Sunday's game against the Panthers.
story: Reed logged limited practice sessions throughout the Lions' Week 4 preparations. The cornerback's status for Sunday's contest remains uncertain as he works through the rib issue he suffered in the Week 3 win over the Jets. If Reed cannot suit up, Rock Ya-Sin will likely start at outside cornerback across from Ennis Rakestraw.

headline: Reed (ribs) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice.
story: Reed presumably picked up the injury during the Lions' 31-24 win over the Jets in Week 3, when he played 62 of 66 defensive snaps (93.9 percent) and finished with eight tackles (five solo) and one pass defense. He'll have two more chances to increase his practice participation to full and avoid an injury designation for Sunday's road game against the Panthers.

headline: Reed (foot) is active for Thursday's game against the Bills.
story: Reed has been battling a foot injury, but he will have the green light to suit up versus Buffalo after carrying a questionable tag heading into the contest. The 29-year-old was heavily involved in the 31-30 overtime win over the Saints in Week 1, amassing 10 total tackles and one pass defended.

headline: Reed (foot) is listed as questionable for Thursday's game against Buffalo.
story: Reed is dealing with a foot injury, so the questionable tag isn't much of a surprise. If Reed can't get on the field versus the Bills, Roger McCreary or Keith Abney could see more action opposite Rock Ya-Sin.

headline: Reed (foot) was limited during Tuesday's practice, Tim Twentyman of the Lions' official site reports.
story: Reed logged 89 snaps in Sunday's 31-30 overtime victory over the Saints, finishing with a team-high 10 tackles (seven solo), as well as a pass defense. If Reed can't suit up for Thursday's meeting with Buffalo, then Roger McCreary or Keith Abney could see an uptick in snaps at outside corner opposite Rock Ya-Sin.

headline: Reed (groin) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice, Tim Twentyman of the Lions' official site reports.
story: Reed dealt with a minor groin issue throughout training camp. The starting outside cornerback for the Lions is healthy and ready to log full sessions in the practices leading up to Sunday's Week 1 contest against the Saints.

headline: Barnes registered eight tackles (five solo) and a defensed pass Sunday in a 31-24 victory against the Jets.
story: Barnes tied with D.J. Reed for the second-most tackles on Detroit behind Christian Izien (11). Barnes has been consistent to begin the campaign, recording between six and eight stops in each of his three games so far. He also has 2.0 sacks on the campaign, halfway to his career-high total over 17 regular-season contests last year.

headline: Barnes recorded seven tackles (five solo), including 1.0 sacks, in Thursday's 41-31 loss to the Bills.
story: The linebacker also had a big day in Week 1, finishing with six tackles (three solo), including 1.0 sacks, and two pass breakups, including an interception. He's off to a strong start to the season despite Detroit's defensive struggles.

headline: Barnes recorded six tackles (three solo), including 1.0 sacks, and two pass defenses (including an interception) during the Lions' 31-30 overtime win over the Saints on Tuesday.
story: Although Barnes wasn't listed as a starter on defense, his 77 defensive snaps were second-most among that position behind only Jack Campbell (90). Barnes set the tone for Detroit right out of halftime, diving in front of a Tyler Shough pass intended for Noah Fant to set the Lions up in Saints territory, leading to a one-yard touchdown run by Jahmyr Gibbs seven plays later. Barnes added a six-yard sack on the Saints' next offensive drive, and the sixth-year pro is off to a terrific start to the 2026 campaign. The Lions' defense will certainly be tested on a short week, hitting the road to take on the Bills on Thursday.

headline: Clark finished Sunday's 31-24 win over the Jets with seven tackles, including 1.0 sacks, and a forced fumble.
story: Clark continues to start at safety for Detroit with with Brian Branch (Achilles) and Kerby Joseph (knee) both on the PUP list. Clark logged just a 45 percent defensive snap share in Week 1, but he upped that to 86 percent in Week 2 before playing every one of the Lions' 61 defensive snaps in Week 3. The veteran defender came up with a huge play late in the contest, sacking Jets QB Geno Smith and causing him to fumble with less than a minute remaining and New York nearing the red zone while trailing by seven points. The sack was Clark's first since he played for the Jets in 2024.

headline: Clark finished with 11 tackles (four solo) in Thursday's 41-31 loss to the Bills.
story: The safety was active on a night when the Lions had trouble stopping the Bills. Clark remains in a starting spot for now with Kerby Joseph (knee) on the reserve/PUP list to begin the season.

headline: Moore (ankle) did not participate at the Packers' practice Wednesday.
story: Moore was sidelined at practice to open the week, as expected. The wide receiver suffered an ankle injury during the team's 31-7 victory over Chicago in Week 5, and he was using a scooter to get around the locker room while his left foot was in a boot Wednesday, per Matt Schneidman of The Athletic. Moore seems unlikely to be available for Week 6, and if he is unable to play, Bo Melton and J. Michael Sturdivant would both be candidates to see an increase in opportunities on offense versus Dallas.

headline: Moore (ankle) wasn't spotted at Wednesday's practice, Bill Huber of SI.com reports.
story: Moore will open Week 6 prep as a non-participant after he made an early exit from this past Sunday's 31-7 win over the Bears due to the ankle injury. He'll have two more chances to potentially get back on the practice field before the Packers decide on his status for this Sunday's game against the Cowboys. If Moore isn't available to play, Bo Melton would likely step in as the Packers' No. 3 wideout behind Christian Watson and Matthew Golden.

headline: The Packers ruled out Moore (ankle) for the remainder of Sunday's game against the Bears.
story: Moore hauled in his lone target for no gain before exiting the contest early in the second quarter. With Moore done for the rest of the afternoon, Bo Melton and J. Michael Sturdivant are expected to serve as the Packers' primary kickoff returners, while Matthew Golden will likely take over on punt returns. The Packers will also rely on Melton and Sturdivant to fill in for Moore at the No. 3 receiver spot.

headline: Moore is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Bears due to an ankle injury.
story: Moore headed to the locker room in the second quarter to receive further evaluation on his ankle injury. Before departing, Moore reeled in his lone target for no gain. If Moore is unable to check back into the game, the Packers will rely on Bo Melton and J. Michael Sturdivant to handle the No. 3 receiver role, while Matthew Golden will likely fill in for Moore on punt returns.

headline: Moore caught one of two targets for minus-2 yards while also adding 52 kickoff-return yards and 19 yards as a punt returner during Sunday's 17-14 win over the Buccaneers.
story: Moore was unable to build off his seven targets from Week 3, garnering his fewest looks since Week 1 in the team's marginal victory versus Tampa Bay. The 26-year-old doesn't carry much upside as a fantasy asset, and he figures to operate as a distant No. 3 option at wide receiver behind Christian Watson and Matthew Golden moving forward.

headline: Coach Matt LaFleur said Wednesday that Moore will be the next man up at wide receiver after it was announced Jayden Reed (neck) will undergo season-ending surgery, Ryan Wood of USA Today reports.
story: With Reed out last Thursday night against the Falcons, Moore played 34 of 66 offensive snaps and ran 27 routes on Jordan Love's 55 dropbacks. Moore caught three of seven targets for 31 yards. He's expected to fight for scraps behind all three of Matthew Golden, Christian Watson and Tucker Kraft in the pecking order for targets.

headline: Moore logged three catches on seven targets for 31 yards while adding 134 yards on five kickoff returns during the Packers' 35-14 loss to the Falcons on Thursday.
story: Moore has seen his playing time on offense steadily increase over the first three games of the regular season, and his 34 snaps on offense Thursday were third-most among wide receivers behind Matthew Golden (54) and Christian Watson (53). Not only were Moore's seven targets third-most among Green Bay wide receivers, they were also a career high for the 2022 second-rounder. The Packers' ground game has struggled due to injuries on the offensive line and the absence of Josh Jacobs (personal), which could mean a higher scoring floor for Moore and the rest of Green Bay's pass catchers.

headline: Moore caught two of three targets for six yards during Sunday's 20-17 overtime win versus the Jets.
story: Moore logged just four snaps in the 39-22 loss to the Vikings in Week 1, though it was a different story in Week 2, with the wideout appearing in 21 of the Packers' 59 offensive snaps against the Jets, finishing behind Christian Watson (53) and Matthew Golden (51) after Jayden Reed (back) lasted just two offensive plays. However, despite the increased workload, Moore didn't do anything meaningful for fantasy managers. That's not expected to change anytime soon, even if Watson or Golden aren't available at some point moving ahead.

headline: Moore failed to catch his only target and returned two punts for 17 yards during Green Bay's loss to the Vikings on Sunday.
story: Moore saw the majority of his playing time on special teams, seeing 11 snaps compared to only four on offense. The 2022 second-round pick of the Chiefs will likely continue to serve as the Packers' primary returner going forward while seeing limited action on offense.

headline: Moore will operate as the Packers' primary retuner on both kicks and punts to open the regular season, Matt Schneidman of The Athletic reports.
story: Moore inked a one-year deal with Green Bay in March, and he'll step in as the team's go-to option on both kicks and punts. The wide receiver notched 907 kickoff-return yards and 291 yards as a punt returner over 17 regular-season contests with San Francisco last year. Moore has combined to catch five of 10 targets for 87 yards over the last two campaigns, so he doesn't carry much fantasy value in 2026.

headline: Wyatt (ankle) has returned to Sunday's game against the buccaneers, Weston Hodkiewicz of the Packers' official site reports.
story: Wyatt briefly left Sunday's game due to an ankle injury, but the fourth-year pro has been cleared by medical staff to return. He'll continue to start alongside Javon Hargrave and Karl Brooks on the defensive line.

headline: Wyatt suffered an ankle injury in Sunday's Week 4 matchup against the Buccaneers and is questionable to return, Ryan Wood of USA Today reports.
story: Wyatt was hurt in the first half. He initially appeared to return to the contest, per Weston Hodkiewicz of the Packers' official site, but was deemed questionable to return shortly thereafter. Chris McClellan could be in line for more defensive snaps if Wyatt is unable to return.

headline: Wyatt (ankle) does not have an injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Jets, Wes Hodkiewicz reports.
story: Wyatt has been dealing with an ankle injury since the start of the regular season. The defensive tackle fractured his ankle in Week 13 of 2025, and it's unclear how closely related his current issue is to that injury. Wyatt was able to play in Week 1 after three limited practices, and he appears firmly on track to do the same in Week 2.

headline: Wyatt (ankle) was a limited participant at the Packers' practice Wednesday.
story: Wyatt was able to play 53 percent of the team's defensive snaps while recording three solo tackles in Green Bay's 39-22 loss to the Vikings in Week 1 after he was limited at practice the entire week. The defensive lineman appears to be on the same track ahead of Week 2, and he'll have two more chances to log a full practice prior to Sunday's matchup with the Jets.

headline: Wyatt (ankle) does not carry an injury designation ahead of Sunday's game at Minnesota, Wes Hodkiewicz of the Packers' official site reports.
story: Wyatt was a limited participant at practice all week because of an issue with his ankle, but it looks like he'll be available in Week 1 anyway. Green Bay will be relying heavily on him to create disruption at the line of scrimmage in 2026, especially until Micah Parsons (knee) is back on the field.

headline: Wyatt (ankle) was a limited participant at the Packers' practice Thursday.
story: Wyatt has logged back-to-back limited practices to open the week with an ankle injury designation. The defensive lineman missed the final five games of the regular season and the Packers' postseason loss to the Bears last year after suffering an ankle fracture in Week 13, and the team is likely just being careful with his health ahead of Sunday's regular-season opener against Minnesota.

headline: Williams (illness) was a limited participant at the Packers' practice Wednesday.
story: Williams is dealing with an illness to open the week, and he was unable to be a full participant at practice as a result. The safety will have two more chances to log a full practice before Sunday night's matchup with the Cowboys.

headline: Williams finished Sunday's 17-14 win over the Buccaneers with seven tackles (three solo), including 1.0 sacks, and two pass defenses (including one interception).
story: Williams picked off undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels midway through the first quarter, and the Packers offense made the most of the takeaway with a 16-play, 68-yard drive that ended with a two-yard touchdown pass from Jordan Love to Matthew Golden. Williams has played every single defensive snap for the Packers, accumulating 34 tackles (20 solo), including 1.0 sacks, and four pass defenses (one interception) through four regular-season games.

headline: Williams recorded 10 tackles (four solo) during Thursday's 35-14 loss to Atlanta.
story: Williams reached double-digit tackles for a second consecutive week, with the third-year safety co-leading the Packers in stops in Thursday's loss. He's up to 27 tackles (17 solo) and two pass defenses through three regular-season games and leads Green Bay in stops, with linebacker Zaire Franklin and Edgerrin Cooper tied for the second-most total tackles on the Packers (21 each).

headline: Williams made 10 tackles (seven solo) and defensed two passes during Sunday's 20-17 overtime win over the Jets.
story: Williams tied Lukas Van Ness for the team lead in tackles during Sunday's contest. The safety played all 72 of the team's defensive snaps in the contest, persevering through the extra period to stop a Jets overtime drive. Williams has not missed a defensive snap in two games and has helped anchor a Packers defense still settling in to the new season.

headline: Nixon recorded five tackles (three solo) including 0.5 sacks and an interception during Sunday's 39-22 loss at Minnesota.
story: Nixon intercepted an ill-advised Kyler Murray pass on the second play of the game from scrimmage, setting up a Packers field goal. He has never recorded more than one interception in a season, and he'll be looking to change that starting in a Week 2 matchup against the Jets.

headline: Monk (quad) is inactive Week 5 against Chicago.
story: Monk will miss his second consecutive game, with hopes of returning Week 6 against the Cowboys. With several recent signings to the Green Bay offensive line, it's unclear what type of role will await Monk once healthy.

headline: Monk (quadriceps) is doubtful to play against the Bears on Sunday.
story: It appears Monk will miss a second consecutive game due to a quad injury that he sustained against the Falcons in Week 3. Aaron Banks (knee/toe) is also listed as doubtful, so the Packers could be light on depth at guard for Sunday's game.

headline: Monk (quadriceps) did not participate at the Packers' practice Thursday.
story: Monk has missed back-to-back practices to open the week as he continues to recover from a quadriceps injury he suffered during the team's Week 3 loss to Atlanta. The 25-year-old appears to be set to miss a second straight game, and Travis Glover could draw another start at left guard Sunday versus Chicago.

headline: Monk (quadriceps) has been ruled out ahead of Sunday's game against the Buccaneers, Wes Hodkiewicz of the Packers' official site reports.
story: Monk was unable to participate in a single practice during the Packers' Week 4 prep. The reserve offensive lineman suffered his injury in the team's Week 3 loss to the Falcons. Donovan Jennings will back up Kevin Zeitler in Sunday's game against the Buccaneers.

headline: Monk picked up an undisclosed injury toward the tail end of the Packers' 35-14 loss to the Falcons on Thursday, Rob Demovsky of ESPN.com reports.
story: Monk was attended to by medical staff during the two-minute warning of the fourth quarter. It's unclear what type of injury he's working through, though the Packers should have an update on the third-year offensive lineman once he undergoes more tests.

headline: Banks (toe) is inactive Week 5 against Chicago.
story: No surprises here, as Banks entered the week with a doubtful tag after only managing to log a single limited practice Friday. Look for Laken Tomlinson to again start in his stead.

headline: Banks (toe/knee) is doubtful for Sunday's game against the Bears, Wes Hodkiewicz of the Packers' official site reports.
story: The good news for Banks is that he returned to practice Friday in a limited capacity, but he'll miss a third consecutive game due to toe and knee injuries. Laken Tomlinson should continue to start at left guard in Banks' absence.

headline: Banks (toe/knee) did not participate at practice Thursday.
story: Banks has sat out the Packers' last two games with toe and knee injuries, and his availability for Week 5 is now also in serious doubt. Unless he's able to practice in some capacity Friday, he'll probably be on track to be sidelined Sunday versus the Bears.

headline: Banks (toe/knee) has been ruled out ahead of Sunday's game against the Buccaneers, Wes Hodkiewicz of the Packers' official site reports.
story: Banks will miss consecutive games due to a toe injury. The starting left guard is now dealing with an additional knee issue and may need to miss even more time. Freshly signed offensive guard Laken Tomlinson is set to start at left guard for the Packers' showdown with the Buccaneers on Sunday.

headline: Banks (toe/knee) did not practice Thursday.
story: Banks hurt his toe in Week 2 against the Jets and didn't play last Thursday versus Atlanta. He also has a knee injury and hasn't practiced at all over the past two weeks. That puts his status for Sunday's matchup against Tampa Bay in serious peril, and Green Bay's practice report Friday should reveal if Banks has even a chance of suiting up.

headline: Banks (toe) has been ruled out ahead of Thursday night's game against the Falcons, Wes Hodkiewicz of the Packers' official site reports.
story: Banks exited the Packers' Week 2 overtime win over the Jets in the second quarter with a toe injury. The left guard was unable to participate in any Week 3 preparation due to the injury. Donovan Jennings is set to start at left guard for Thursday's game.

headline: Banks (toe) has been ruled out for the remainder of Sunday's game against the Jets.
story: The starting left guard exited Sunday's contest in the second quarter after sustaining a toe injury. Banks will not return, leaving Jager Burton to slot in at guard due to Donovan Jennings' (hand) injury.

headline: Banks (toe) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Jets.
story: Banks sustained the injury in the second quarter of Sunday's game. Donovan Jennings has taken over at left guard and will remain there unless Banks is cleared to return.

headline: Banks (knee) is active for Sunday's game against the Jets, Mike Spofford of the Packers' official site reports.
story: Banks was limited in practice throughout Week 2. The starting left guard has recovered from his knee injury enough to suit up for Sunday's game.

headline: Banks (knee) is listed as questionable ahead of Sunday's game against the Jets, Wes Hodkiewicz of the Packers' official site reports.
story: Banks was a limited participant in practice throughout Week 2 prep. The starting left guard was unable to suit up for the Packers' Week 1 loss to the Vikings due to his knee injury, despite following the same practice regimen. Unless Banks has made significant improvement, it seems there's a possibility he'll miss a second straight game Sunday.

headline: Banks (knee) was a limited participant in practice Thursday.
story: The starting left guard was limited Wednesday as well after missing Green Bay's Week 1 loss to Minnesota. Banks was also unable to fully practice ahead of that contest. Donovan Jennings is Green Bay's first backup guard in case Banks can't go this Sunday against the Jets.

headline: Banks (knee) is inactive for Sunday's game against Minnesota.
story: Banks drew the questionable tag for Sunday's regular-season opener due to knee tendinitis that limited him in practice all week. However, he has not been cleared to play after going through pregame warmups, and he'll shift his focus toward being available for Week 2 against the Jets on Sunday, Sept. 20. Jager Burton figures to start at left guard in Banks' absence.

headline: Banks (knee) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Vikings, Wes Hodkiewicz of the Packers' official site reports.
story: Banks continues to battle a case of knee tendinitis, logging three consecutive limited practice sessions in Week 1. Coach Matt LaFleur indicated Wednesday that the limited sessions were just for rest and that the left guard will start Sunday regardless of his current injury designation and practice status.

headline: Banks (knee) was limited during Wednesday's practice, Ryan Wood of USA Today reports.
story: Banks is battling a case of tendinitis. Head coach Matt LaFleur indicated Banks would start regardless of how much practice time he gets ahead of Sunday's matchup with Minnesota, meaning he may remain limited for the rest of the week.

headline: Campbell (ankle) is inactive Week 5 against Chicago.
story: Campbell has played just 10 total snaps all season, missing three of the first four games, so it should still be business as usual for the Green Bay defensive line without him.

headline: Campbell (ankle) has been ruled out ahead of Sunday's game against the Buccaneers, Wes Hodkiewicz of the Packers' official site reports.
story: Campbell did not participate in any Week 4 prep sessions for the Packers. The defensive tackle remains sidelined with the ankle injury he suffered in the Packers' Week 2 overtime win over the Jets.

headline: Campbell (ankle) is inactive for Thursday Night Football against the Falcons, Mike Spofford of the Packers' official site reports.
story: The defensive lineman exited Green Bay's overtime win over the Jets early last Sunday due to an ankle injury, but he returned to practice on a limited basis Tuesday and Wednesday. Nevertheless, the issue appears to still be serious enough to hold Campbell out for Thursday's matchup.

headline: Campbell (ankle) was listed as a non-participant in Monday's estimated practice report, Tom Silverstein of the Milwaukee Journal Sentinel reports.
story: Campbell exited the Sunday overtime win against the Jets early. The reserve defensive lineman for the Packers was unable to return to the game due to an ankle injury and was projected to have been unable to practice Monday had Green Bay held an official session. The 26-year-old will need to upgrade his participation level by Wednesday for any chance to suit up in Thursday night's game against the Falcons.

headline: Campbell (ankle) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Jets.
story: It's unclear when Campbell sustained the injury, but he's being monitored by medical staff to determine whether he can return to Sunday's contest. Chris McClellan will see a slight bump in snaps at defensive end in a rotational role for as long as Campbell is out of the game.

headline: Jennings (hand) does not have any injury designation ahead of Thursday night's game against the Falcons, Wes Hodkiewicz of the Packers' official site reports.
story: Jennings did not participate in Monday's estimated practice due to a hand injury. The left guard upgraded to limited participation in Tuesday and Wednesday's sessions, clearing the way for his start at left guard Thursday in Aaron Banks' (toe) absence.

headline: Jennings (hand) did not participate in Monday's estimated practice, Tom Silverstein of the Milwaukee Journal Sentinel reports.
story: Jennings suffered a hand injury in Sunday's overtime win over the Jets. The reserve offensive lineman for the Packers likely won't suit up for Thursday's game against the Falcons unless he can rapidly recover from the injury.

headline: Jennings (hand) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Jets.
story: Jennings was in the game at left guard for Aaron Banks (toe), the latter of whom is also questionable to return. Jager Burton has taken over at left guard in the absences of both Banks and Jennings.

headline: The Packers aren't planning on opening Parsons' (knee) 21-day practice window this week ahead of Sunday's game against the Cowboys, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
story: Parsons had previously noted in the early stages of training camp that the Week 6 matchup with his former team was a realistic target for his season debut. The 27-year-old ultimately won't be ready to play against Dallas, and while the Packers remain hopeful he'll be able to return to action at some point in October, his absence looks increasingly likely to stretch into November since he has yet to resume practicing with the team. Green Bay hasn't indicated that Parsons has experienced any setbacks from the torn ACL in his left knee that he sustained Dec. 14, as the team may simply be taking a deliberate approach with the star pass rusher's recovery.

headline: Parsons (knee), per head coach Matt LaFleur, will not practice this week, Weston Hodkiewicz of the Packers' official site reports.
story: With four weeks in the books, Parsons now is eligible to be activated from the reserve/PUP list, but with him not yet ready to practice he will not return to action in Week 5 against the Bears, and it may be tough for him to make it back for Green Bay's Week 6 matchup against his former Dallas team.

headline: Packers head coach Matt LaFleur said Monday that Parsons (knee) hasn't experienced any setbacks but won't be cleared to practice this week, Rob Demovsky of ESPN.com reports.
story: Because he was placed on the PUP list July 28, Parsons has been eligible to resume practicing since Week 2, but the Packers aren't yet ready to open his 21-day evaluation window. Parsons had previously told Ryan Wood of USA Today that the Packers' Oct. 18 game against the Cowboys was a "very realistic" target for him to make his 2026 debut, but in order for that to happen, the star edge rusher would likely have to start practicing by next week.

headline: Packers general manager Brian Gutekunst said Tuesday that Parsons (knee) could return from the PUP list when first eligible in Week 5, Ryan Wood of USA Today reports. "We have a pretty good idea once we get out of that four-game window we're going to be pretty close," Gutekunst said.
story: Though he'll miss time to begin the season, Parsons is progressing as expected in his recovery from a torn ACL in his left knee, which he sustained Dec. 14. Parsons had previously told Wood that the Packers' Week 6 game against the Cowboys was a "very realistic" target for his return to the field, and Gutekunst's comments suggest that the door is open for the star edge rusher to play as soon as Week 5 against the Bears. According to Matt Schneidman of The Athletic, Gutekunst added that Parsons could be a candidate to resume practicing as soon as Week 2, when the Packers would first be able to open up his 21-day evaluation window.

headline: The Packers moved Parsons (knee) from the active/PUP list to the reserve/PUP list Sunday, meaning he'll miss the first four games of the season, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
story: Parsons was lost for the 2025 season Week 15 when he sustained a torn ACL in his left knee, but not before fulfilling expectations following his blockbuster arrival from Dallas prior to Week 1. Overall, he recorded 12.5 sacks in 14 regular-season contests, marking his fifth straight campaign to begin his career with at least 12.0 sacks. Based on comments made by Parsons to Ryan Wood of USA Today on Aug. 4, the pass rusher is aiming to return Week 6, but with Sunday's transaction, his first possible return date is a Week 5 matchup with the Bears.

headline: Strong took the field for 24 of the Packers' 59 offensive snaps in Sunday's 31-7 win over the Bears, finishing with five carries for seven yards and three catches for 11 yards on four targets.
story: Signed off the practice squad Thursday, Strong made his Packers debut three days later and ended up settling in as the No. 2 option in the backfield behind MarShawn Lloyd, who played just two more snaps but handily out-produced him (10-31-2 rushing line, one catch for six yards). Meanwhile, after committing a costly goal-line fumble in the Week 4 win over the Buccaneers, Kaleb Johnson logged just nine snaps and gained 26 yards on his seven carries. As the more capable option on passing downs, Strong looks like he could continue to work ahead of Johnson while Chris Brooks (ankle) is on injured reserve.

headline: The Packers signed Strong (hamstring) to their active roster from their practice squad Thursday.
story: Strong was tending to a hamstring injury early in the season, but now he's presumably back in game shape. Green Bay is last in rushing offense by a wide margin through the first four weeks of the season, so there's plenty of incentive for the team not to afford Strong some opportunities once he has acclimated himself. Over 14 regular-season games with the Browns in 2024, he carried the ball 26 times for 108 yards, and he caught 14 of 22 targets for 104 yards.

headline: Strong, who is on Green Bay's practice squad, is currently managing a hamstring issue, Bill Huber of SI.com reports.
story: Strong had been a candidate to be elevated for the Packers' season opener Sunday versus Minnesota since Josh Jacobs is on the Commissioner's Exempt List, but that's presumably no longer in play. It's not clear how severe Strong's injury is, and given that Jacobs could be out multiple games, Strong could still be a gameday practice-squad elevation down the line once he gets healthy.

headline: The Packers signed Strong to the practice squad Monday.
story: The Packers released Strong on Sunday as part of the team's effort to reach an initial 53-man roster. The running back promptly rejoined the team and will look to prove himself as worthy of elevation to the active roster if MarShawn Lloyd, Chris Brooks or Kaleb Johnson must miss time with injury.

headline: Strong was cut by the Packers on Sunday, Tom Silverstein of the Milwaukee Journal Sentinel reports.
story: Strong fell out of the Packers' plans when Green Bay traded for Steelers running back Kaleb Johnson on Sunday. The 27-year-old Strong has appeared in 46 regular-season games, split between the Patriots and Browns, though he hasn't dressed for one since the 2024 campaign.

headline: Taylor played the final two snaps of Sunday's 31-7 win over the Bears, losing two yards on a pair of kneeldowns.
story: Signed to a one-year, $2.5 million deal in May to serve as Jordan Love's backup, Taylor was summoned off the bench for his first snaps of the season as the Packers closed out a blowout win. So long as Love stays healthy, Taylor's appearances will be limited to garbage-time situations throughout the season.

headline: MRI tests Monday confirmed that Hargrave tore his Achilles during the Packers' 31-7 win over the Bears on Sunday, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
story: It's another brutal blow to the Packers defense, which lost linebacker Edgerrin Cooper to the same injury in Week 4 against the Buccaneers. The next step for Hargrave is season-ending surgery, and the recovery timeline could keep the veteran defensive lineman sidelined for part of the 2027 campaign. With both Hargrave and Jordon Riley (Achilles, PUP) done for the year, 2022 seventh-rounder Jonathan Ford figures to see a significant jump in snaps on the defensive line for the rest of the 2026 season.

headline: Packers head coach Matt LaFleur said after Sunday's 31-7 win over the Bears that Hargrave sustained a season-ending torn Achilles, Bill Huber of SI.com reports.
story: Green Bay will send Hargrave in for an MRI to confirm the injury, but the veteran defensive lineman is fully expected to require season-ending surgery to repair the damaged tendon. Hargrave went down with the injury late in the fourth quarter in what ended up being a bittersweet ending to an impressive win for Green Bay. The 33-year-old defensive tackle, who joined Green Bay on a two-year deal in March, will finish his first season in green and gold with six stops and one pass breakup over four games.

headline: Hargrave (undisclosed) was carted off the field in the final minutes of Sunday's game against the Bears, Matt Schneidman of The Athletic reports.
story: Since Hargrave suffered his injury near the end of the game, he never received an official injury designation. The defensive tackle being carted off the field signals the injury is likely significant.

headline: Hargrave (toe) is active Week 5 against the Bears.
story: Hargrave entered the week with a questionable designation after only logging a single limited practice, but the veteran nose tackle will ultimately suit up for what the team is hoping is his regular role in the defensive line rotation.

headline: Hargrave (toe) is listed as questionable against the Bears on Sunday, Wes Hodkiewicz of the Packers' official site reports.
story: The toe injury appears to be a new one for Hargrave, who popped up on Friday's injury report as a limited practice participant. His official status may not be known until the Packers announce their list of inactive players approximately 90 minutes before the 1:00 p.m. ET kickoff. Jonathan Ford and rookie third-rounder Chris McClellan would both operate in elevated roles if Hargrave is unable to play.

headline: Hargrave (concussion/knee) is active for Thursday Night Football against the Falcons, Mike Spofford of the Packers' official site reports.
story: The defensive tackle entered the day with a questionable tag after practicing on a limited basis during the week leading up to the game. Hargrave had to be cleared by an independent neurologist for full contact to have a chance to play Thursday night, and it appears that he has gotten that clearance. The veteran should be ready to start at nose tackle.

headline: Hargrave (concussion/knee) is listed as questionable ahead of Thursday night's game against the Falcons, Wes Hodkiewicz of the Packers' official site reported Wednesday.
story: Hargrave logged limited participation throughout the Packers' Week 3 practices as he deals with both a knee injury and a concussion. The starting nose tackle will need to be cleared by an independent neurologist for full contact by Thursday's game to be able to suit up.

headline: Hargrave (concussion/knee) has been ruled out ahead of Sunday's game against the Jets.
story: Hargrave was listed as doubtful after Friday's practice, so it is no surprise that the nose tackle has been ruled out ahead of Sunday's contest. The 33-year-old was able to log only one limited practice session throughout Week 2, meaning he will still need to upgrade to full participation and clear the NFL's five-step concussion protocol in Week 3 before even thinking about stepping back on a game-day field.

headline: Hargrave (concussion/knee) is listed as doubtful ahead of Sunday's game against the Jets, Wes Hodkiewicz reports.
story: Hargrave was a limited participant in Wednesday's session as he worked through a concussion and a knee issue. The starting nose tackle then missed the Thursday and Friday's sessions. It now appears Hargrave will not suit up for Sunday's game against the Jets, but if he's able to play, he would need to be vetted by an independent neurologist to clear the NFL's five-step concussion protocol.

headline: Hargrave (knee/concussion) did not participate in practice Thursday.
story: The defensive tackle was limited Wednesday. Hargrave played on 29 defensive snaps and one special-teams snap last week against Minnesota, making one tackle. If he can't go Sunday, Jonathan Ford is the next man up at nose tackle.

headline: Hargrave (knee/concussion) was limited during Wednesday's practice.
story: Hargrave had one total tackle in Sunday's 39-22 loss to the Vikings. He's currently dealing with multiple injuries. If Hargrave isn't on the field in Week 2 versus the Jets, Jonathan Ford could see more snaps.

headline: Hargrave (knee) does not carry an injury designation ahead of Sunday's game at Minnesota, Wes Hodkiewicz of the Packers' official site reports.
story: Hargrave was limited at practice all week by a knee issue, but it won't keep him off the field in Week 1. To the extent that the veteran's stamina and health allows, he figures to see plenty of work on Green Bay's defensive line in 2026.

headline: Hargrave (knee) was a limited participant at the Packers' practice Thursday.
story: Hargrave has opened the week with back-to-back limited practices as he continues to work his way back from a knee injury that sidelined him for the entirety of training camp. The defensive tackle will have one more chance to log a full practice Friday before potentially making his regular-season debut with the Packers on Sunday against Minnesota.

headline: Smack went 1-for-3 on field-goal attempts and 2-for-3 on extra-point tries during the Packers' 31-7 win over the Bears on Sunday.
story: Smack missed field goals from 43 and 47 yards in the fourth quarter, which came after his extra-point try early in the third missed wide left. It was by far the worst performance of the rookie's young NFL career, but luckily for him, the Packers dominated enough offensively and defensively that his kicking miscues were a wash. Smack will have a prime opportunity to bounce back in Week 6 on Oct. 18 against the Cowboys, who give up the seventh-most points in the NFL this season (27.2).

headline: Smack made his only field-goal attempt and both of his PATs during Sunday's 17-14 win over Tampa Bay.
story: Smack had only one opportunity to kick a field goal in Week 4, but he made the most of it. The rookie nailed a 58-yard attempt as time expired in the first half, delivering the Packers a 10-7 lead at the break. Smack's field goal would prove to be the difference in a low-scoring battle. On the year, the kicker has gone 6-for-7 on field-goal tries, including 3-for-3 from 50-plus yards, over four contests so far.

headline: Smack went 0-for-1 on field-goal tries and 2-for-2 on extra-point attempts in Thursday's 35-14 loss to the Falcons.
story: The kicker's 47-yard attempt in the second quarter was blocked. It was Smack's first miss on a field-goal try this season, and it probably wasn't his fault. The rookie has, however, missed an extra point as well.

headline: Smack made both of his field-goal attempts and went 2-for-2 on extra-point tries during the Packers' 20-17 overtime win over the Jets on Sunday.
story: Smack's 34-yard field goal late in the fourth quarter tied things up at 17-17 before the rookie sealed the game for the Packers with a 26-yard chip shot in overtime. The rookie sixth-rounder is off to a strong start to his NFL career, having gone 5-for-5 on field-goal tries and 3-for-4 on extra-point attempts across the first two games of the regular season.

headline: Smack made all three of his field-goal attempts while missing one of two PATs in Sunday's 39-22 loss to the Vikings.
story: Smack made field goals from 59, 43 and 26 yards but fell short of a flawless night after missing an extra-point try. The sixth-round rookie had a strong debut overall with 10 total points.

headline: Smack went 4-of-4 on field goals and 3-of-3 on extra points in Friday's 33-13 preseason victory over the Broncos.
story: Smack made all three field goals he got up -- including a 58-yarder -- in last week's exhibition opener, and the rookie remained perfect thanks to an ever better night that included makes from both 51 and 59 yards out. Packers kickers haven't been particularly fantasy-friendly in recent years, but if Smack remains true from long range he has a chance to change that.

headline: Why Mike Clay is not interested in MarShawn Lloyd in Week 6
story: Why Mike Clay is not interested in MarShawn Lloyd in Week 6

headline: Lloyd rushed 10 times for 31 yards and two touchdowns while catching one of two targets for six yards during Sunday's 31-7 win over the Bears.
story: Lloyd was able to open the second quarter with a 10-yard touchdown run before later adding a four-yard score in the fourth quarter. The running back's 10 carries were his most since logging 13 rushes for 37 yards in Week 1 versus Minnesota. Lloyd has now compiled 112 rushing yards on 40 carries and two touchdowns while reeling in 10 of 13 targets for 55 yards and a score over five games to open the 2026 season while operating as Green Bay's primary option in the backfield with Josh Jacobs (personal) on the Commissioner's Exempt List.

headline: Lloyd rushed seven times for 13 yards and brought in all five targets for 36 yards in the Packers' 17-14 win over the Buccaneers on Sunday.
story: It was more of the same on the ground for Lloyd, who barely eclipsed the season-low 11 rushing yards he produced in Week 3 against the Falcons. However, the third-year back set new career highs in receptions, receiving yards and targets, offering some modest fantasy value on the afternoon. Lloyd's backfield mate Kaleb Johnson led the ground attack with eight carries for 42 yards Sunday, and although Lloyd remains largely ineffective as a runner, he'll likely remain in a relevant role in Week 5 at home against the Bears if the ankle injury that forced Chris Brooks' exit from the contest keeps him sidelined for that divisional contest.

headline: Lloyd rushed four times for 11 yards and brought in two of three targets for seven yards in the Packers' 35-14 loss to the Falcons on Thursday.
story: The inefficiency reflected in his final line underscores the type of season it's been so far for Lloyd, who's tried in vain to serve as a serviceable replacement for Josh Jacobs (personal) while he remains on the Commissioner's Exempt List. Lloyd's rushing opportunities were limited Thursday largely due to game script, but the 2024 third-round pick is averaging just 3.0 yards per carry through three games and has complemented it with an unremarkable 4-13-0 line through the air. Lloyd, Chris Brooks and Kaleb Johnson will continue to share the Packers' backfield workload in a Week 4 road matchup against the Buccaneers on Sunday, Oct. 4.

headline: Lloyd rushed six times for 20 yards in the Packers' 20-17 overtime win over the Jets on Sunday. He added two catches for six yards and a touchdown on two targets.
story: Lloyd got the start out of the backfield for Green Bay and scored his first career regular-season touchdown with a six-yard catch in the second quarter. That's the good news. The bad news is Lloyd played a total of just 16 offensive snaps and lost a fumble deep in his own territory early in the fourth quarter. He never touched the ball again following the fumble, as Kaleb Johnson took over as the early-down back in overtime, with Chris Brooks remaining the preferred option in passing situations. Lloyd gets a dream matchup with the Falcons on Thursday night, but it's fair to wonder about his role headed into that Week 3 contest.

headline: Lloyd rushed 13 times for 37 yards and didn't catch his lone target in Sunday's 39-22 loss to the Vikings.
story: Lloyd worked ahead of Chris Brooks (seven carries for 29 yards) in a Packers backfield that struggled to generate much in the absence of Josh Jacobs (personal), who is on the Commissioner's Exempt List. Jordan Love threw 42 passes compared to 20 combined carries for Lloyd and Brooks, even though Green Bay led for most of the game prior to being outscored 22-0 in the fourth quarter. Lloyd looks poised to handle double-digit touches again in Week 2 against the Jets.

headline: Packers offensive coordinator Adam Stenavich suggested Tuesday that Lloyd could be part of a backfield committee to begin the season while Josh Jacobs (personal) remains on the Commissioner's Exempt List, Weston Hodkiewicz of the Packers' official site reports. "It's gonna be running back by committee for a little bit to see where everyone is at," Stenavich said. "[Lloyd] definitely has explosive ability, playmaking ability."
story: Though he profiles as the most enticing fantasy option of a backfield group that includes Kaleb Johnson and Chris Brooks, Lloyd doesn't look like he'll be called upon to handle a workhorse role during Jacobs' absence. While Lloyd made it through training camp and the preseason healthy and flashed his upside as both a ball carrier and pass catcher, durability has not been his string suit in the NFL. The 2024 third-round pick been limited to just one career game on account of multiple soft-tissue injuries, in addition to an emergency appendectomy.

headline: With both Josh Jacobs (groin) landing on the Commissioner's Exempt List and Kaleb Johnson being acquired by the Packers on Sunday, Lloyd now finds himself in a reconfigured Packers backfield.
story: Lloyd has appeared in just one regular-season game since being selected by the Packers in the third round of the 2024 NFL Draft, but with Jacobs out of action for the time being Lloyd is now the top available option on the depth chart. Both Johnson and Chris Brooks -- who excels at pass blocking -- figure to factor into the mix sans Jacobs, but with Johnson just joining the team, Lloyd now finds himself as the favorite to pick up carries.

headline: Lloyd rushed six times for 17 yards and secured his only target for an 11-yard touchdown in the Packers' 33-13 preseason win over the Broncos on Friday.
story: Josh Jacobs (groin) was not in uniform Friday, paving the way for Lloyd to see meaningful early-game action for the second straight preseason contest. Lloyd found tough sledding on the ground against a talented Denver defense, but he capped off the Packers' opening drive with his 11-yard touchdown reception. Lloyd may have the inside track to the No. 2 running back role despite playing just one regular-season game in his first two seasons, although that may not be official until the Packers' preseason finale next Friday at home against the Cardinals.

headline: Kraft brought in all five targets for 64 yards and rushed once for two yards in the Packers' 31-7 win over the Bears on Sunday.
story: Kraft was an ideal complementary piece alongside top receivers Christian Watson and Matthew Golden, who combined for 12 receptions for 266 yards and two touchdowns (Watson) on the afternoon. Kraft still managed to finish with his second-highest reception and receiving yardage totals of the season, and he should remain busy in what is likely to be a high-scoring Week 6 home showdown against the Cowboys next Sunday night.

headline: Kraft brought in six of seven targets for 42 yards and a touchdown in the Packers' 17-14 win over the Buccaneers on Sunday. He also rushed once for three yards.
story: Kraft set the pace for the Packers in receptions and tied with Matthew Golden for the team lead in targets on the afternoon while also finishing as the runner-up in receiving yards for Green Bay. The talented tight end also notched his first touchdown of the season with a two-yard catch early in the second half that was originally ruled out of bounds before being overturned on replay. Kraft has made a remarkable recovery from last year's season-ending knee injury, producing a 15-148-1 line over his first four games heading into a Week 5 home matchup against the Bears next Sunday.

headline: Kraft secured four of eight targets for 26 yards in the Packers' 35-14 loss to the Falcons on Thursday. He also recovered a fumble.
story: Kraft finished third in targets and catches on the night for the Packers, but in uncharacteristic fashion, the field-stretching tight end was limited to a short-area role. He made an impressively rapid recovery from last year's torn ACL, which he suffered Week 9 of the 2025 campaign, to open the season in his customary No. 1 tight end role. However, he's mustered a modest a 9-106-0 line on 17 targets through three games heading into a Week 4 road matchup against the Buccaneers on Sunday, Oct. 4.

headline: Kraft caught two of three targets for 15 yards in Sunday's 20-17 overtime win over the Jets.
story: Kraft was one of five Packers to put the ball on the ground in slick conditions Sunday, but four of those fumbles were recovered by Green Bay, including Kraft's miscue. The star tight end has just five catches for 80 yards through two games in his return from a torn ACL suffered in Week 9 of last season. Prior to the injury, Kraft averaged over 60 yards per game and scored six times in eight games during the 2025 regular season. He may still be working his way back to 100 percent heading into Thursday's Week 3 home game against the struggling Falcons.

headline: Kraft caught three of six targets for 65 yards in Sunday's 39-22 loss to the Vikings.
story: Kraft avoided the Week 1 injury report in his return from a torn ACL suffered Week 9 of last season. He finished third on the team in receiving yards in his return, behind wide receivers Christian Watson (147 yards) and Matthew Golden (95 yards). Kraft is poised to maintain a prominent role Week 2 against the Jets.

headline: Kraft and the Packers reached an agreement on a four-year, $75 million contract extension worth up to $92 million Saturday, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
story: The deal includes a $26.5 million signing bonus, making Kraft the NFL's highest-paid tight end and under contract with the Packers through 2030, per Jeremy Fowler of ESPN.com. Kraft was one of the most productive tight ends through the first half of the 2025 regular season before his campaign abruptly ended in Week 9 due to a torn ACL. He's not on the injury report for Sunday's regular-season opener against the Vikings, and the 2023 third-rounder is expected to be one of the top targets for Jordan Love in the passing game, alongside fellow tight end Jonnu Smith and wide receivers Christian Watson, Jayden Reed and Matthew Golden.

headline: Kraft (knee) is not listed on the Packers' Week 1 injury report Wednesday, Tom Silverstein of the Milwaukee Journal Sentinel reports.
story: Kraft has been working in full pads for weeks, so it's no surprise. He's ready to go for Sunday's game against the Vikings and is a top-five TE1 for fantasy in that matchup.

headline: Kraft (knee) is in full pads at Wednesday's practice, Matt Schneidman of The Athletic reports.
story: Kraft has been in full pads at practice for weeks and appears ready to go for Sunday's Week 1 opener against the Vikings. He's insisted he's ready and doesn't need to be on a snap count, but it will be something to watch Sunday in Kraft's first game back from a torn ACL. Even if he's somewhat limited, Kraft is a locked-in fantasy TE1.

headline: Kraft (knee) appeared to be running without any limitations during Wednesday's practice, Matt Schneidman of The Athletic reports.
story: Though Kraft was held out of action during the Packers' entire preseason slate, he was able to clear a major hurdle in his recovery from the torn ACL he sustained Nov. 2, 2025 by taking contact in a joint practice with the Cardinals last week. Kraft appeared to be in full uniform and pads for Wednesday's session, suggesting that he's on track to be ready to go for the Packers' Week 1 matchup with the Vikings. Green Bay will release its first injury report of 2026 next Wednesday, and if Kraft is listed as a full participant or is off the report entirely, it would provide confirmation that he's been cleared to play in the season opener.

headline: Kraft (knee) is expected to be "full go" for the Packers' Week 1 regular-season opener against the Vikings, Rob Demovsky of ESPN.com reports.
story: Kraft got his first taste of full contact in joint practice with the Cardinals on Wednesday, and he deemed himself ready to go for the start of the 2026 season. The tight end isn't going to play in Friday's preseason finale, so all sights are set on Week 1. Kraft will be 10 months removed from his torn ACL next week after he sustained the injury in Week 9 against the Panthers last season.

headline: Kraft (knee) will participate in team drills during Wednesday's joint practice with the Cardinals, Ryan Wood of USA Today reports.
story: Kraft has been participating in team drills for over a week, and he has advanced enough to get some work in against an opposing team. It's still not certain that Kraft will be ready for Week 1, and it was reported earlier in August that he could open on a snap count even if he is ready to go, but the chances of him both being out there and filling a key role continue to rise.

headline: Kraft (knee) has been impressive in 11-on-11 drills since the Packers cleared him Sunday to take part in them at practice, Bill Huber of SI.com reports
story: Since that point, Kraft has been making plays against the Packers defense, recording four catches Sunday and five more Tuesday. One of those grabs occurred on a deep ball down the right side from QB Jordan Love, who arced a pass over CB Keisean Nixon that Kraft hauled in with one hand and then sprinted for a would-be touchdown. This comes on the heels of Kraft telling Rob Demovsky of ESPN.com on Sunday that he hopes to not be on a snap count to begin the season but acknowledged that the Packers may place him on one following last November's ACL tear. Meanwhile, Kraft and the Packers still are aiming to lock in a contract extension before Week 1.

headline: Kraft said Sunday that he expects the Packers to limit his reps "probably until halfway through the season," Rob Demovsky of ESPN.com reports.
story: Kraft has been trending toward returning Week 1 following a season-ending torn ACL suffered during Week 9 of the 2025 campaign, and he also returned to 11-on-11 drills for the first time Sunday. The fourth-year tight end added that he's hoping not to be on a rep count for the regular-season opener, per Demovsky, so it'll be worth monitoring his status leading into that game versus the Vikings on Sunday, Sept. 13. Kraft played at least 88 percent of the Packers' offensive snaps in each of their first seven games before going down last year. He finished with 32 catches for 489 yards and six touchdowns over eight contests in 2025. Kraft also was asked whether he expects a new contract by Week 1, saying "that's the goal," according to Matt Schneidman of The Athletic.

headline: Head coach Matt LaFleur told reporters that Kraft (knee) will participate in 11-on-11 team drills during Sunday's training camp practice, Matt Schneidman of The Athletic reports.
story: Kraft opened training camp on the active/PUP list but has slowly increased his workload over the course of the last couple of weeks. His clearance to work in team drills is another positive step in his recovery from a torn ACL that he sustained in Week 9 of the 2025 season. Kraft is unlikely to play in either of the Packers' last two preseason games but appears to be on track to suit up Week 1 against the Vikings on Sunday, Sept. 13.

headline: Why Dopp is locking Jordan Love in as a top-7 QB in Week 6
story: Why Dopp is locking Jordan Love in as a top-7 QB in Week 6

headline: Love completed 25 of 31 passes for 367 yards with two touchdowns and no interceptions while adding one carry for six yards in the Packers' 31-7 win over the Bears on Sunday. He also fumbled once but recovered.
story: Love was in prime form all afternoon against the Packers' long-time arch-rival, finishing with the third-highest single-game passing yardage total of his career while facilitating 100-yard efforts for both Christian Watson and Matthew Golden. The veteran signal-caller connected with the former for both of his touchdown passes, which came from 42 and 53 yards out in the first and third quarters, respectively. Love already has a trio of 300-yard games on the season and a 10:3 TD:INT heading into a Week 6 home matchup against the Cowboys next Sunday night.

headline: Love completed 22 of 30 passes for 197 yards with two touchdowns and one interception and rushed four times for minus-8 yards in the Packers' 17-14 win over the Buccaneers on Sunday.
story: Love's final line was a serviceable one despite the low-scoring and often choppy game, and the veteran signal-caller salvaged his fantasy day with touchdown tosses of two yards each to Matthew Golden and Tucker Kraft. Love spread the ball around to eight different targets overall on the afternoon, and although he's completed a career-low 56.5 percent of his passes through four games, he also boasts an 8:3 TD:INT in that span. Love next takes on the division-rival Bears in a Week 5 home matchup next Sunday.

headline: Love completed 28 of 53 passes for 312 yards with two touchdowns and one interception and rushed once for no gain in the Packers' 35-14 loss to the Falcons on Thursday. He also committed a fumble recovered by Green Bay.
story: While Love's final line was certainly a fantasy-friendly one, it was largely the byproduct of Green Bay being playing catch-up in the fourth quarter and the Falcons showing a willingness to give up some yardage while in prevent mode. Love spread the ball around to nine different targets on the night, and he connected with Christian Watson (four yards) and Matthew Golden (15 yards ) -- who were his two most prolific options by far -- for his pair of touchdown passes. Love's one interception closed out the Packers' final drive with the game already out of reach, but the embattled veteran signal-caller does head into a Week 4 road matchup against the Buccaneers on Sunday, Oct. 4 averaging 281.3 passing yards per game while sporting a 6:2 TD:INT.

headline: Love completed 16 of 29 passes for 145 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 20-17 overtime win over the Jets.
story: The Packers struggled to move the ball for most of the afternoon but benefited from some key penalties as they came back from a 17-7 fourth-quarter deficit to win a sloppily played game in rainy conditions. Love got the scoring started with a six-yard touchdown pass to MarShawn Lloyd just under 10 minutes before halftime, but Green Bay's next points didn't come until Love's three-yard touchdown pass to Christian Watson with 7:58 left in the fourth quarter. Green Bay did just enough to avoid starting 0-2 heading into Thursday's Week 3 home game against the Falcons, but Love has an uninspiring 52 percent completion percentage after completing 66.3 percent of his passes during the 2025 regular season.

headline: Love completed 21 of 42 passes for 387 yards, two touchdowns and one interception in Sunday's 39-22 loss to the Vikings. He also rushed once for no gain and fumbled twice, losing one.
story: Love started hot, connecting with Christian Watson for an 81-yard touchdown in the first quarter and a two-yard touchdown in the final minute of the first half. Green Bay's offense sputtered in the second half, and both of Love's turnovers came in the fourth quarter, during which the Vikings outscored the Packers, 22-0. Love finished with the second-highest passing yards total of his career, trailing only his 389-yard performance in a Week 4 loss to the Vikings in 2024, and he exceeded 42 pass attempts only once in 15 regular-season starts last season. Green Bay may continue to rely heavily on Love's arm as long as Josh Jacobs (personal) is on the Commissioner's Exempt List, which may remain the case Week 2 against the Jets.

headline: Golden secured six of seven targets for 123 yards in the Packers' 31-7 win over the Bears on Sunday. He also returned two punts for 27 yards.
story: As good as Golden's afternoon was, he was actually slightly outshined by fellow wideout Christian Watson, who had 20 more receiving yards on the same number of catches and one additional target. Nevertheless, Golden's afternoon included a new career high in receiving yards, as well as a career-high-tying reception total. The second-year speedster is already well on his way to a breakout campaign, and he now has had at least seven targets in four of his first five games. The 2025 first-round pick will take a 24-397-2 line on 44 targets into a favorable Week 6 home matchup against the Cowboys next Sunday night.

headline: Golden brought in three of seven targets for 21 yards and a touchdown in the Packers' 17-14 win over the Buccaneers on Sunday. He also rushed once for six yards.
story: Jordan Love threw for a modest 197 yards overall on the afternoon, so Golden's subdued production can be viewed within that context. The second-year speedster tied with Tucker Kraft for the team lead in targets on the afternoon, and although Golden brought in less than half of them. he recorded his second touchdown grab of the campaign on a two-yard reception early in the second quarter. Golden's reception and yardage totals were season lows, but he's still on pace for a breakout second campaign with an 18-274-2 line going into a Week 5 home divisional matchup against the Bears next Sunday.

headline: Golden brought in five of 12 targets for 100 yards and a touchdown in the Packers' 35-14 loss to the Falcons on Thursday.
story: Golden set the pace for the Packers in both receiving yards and targets with totals that also qualified as or tied new single-game career highs. The second-year wideout has hit the ground running this season, quickly generating a 15-253-1 line on 30 targets while showing clearly improved chemistry with Jordan Love. The speedster also added his first touchdown catch of the campaign on an impressive 15-yard grab in the fourth quarter where Golden had to reach behind him to reel in the ball, and he'll remain a coveted option in all fantasy formats in a Week 4 road matchup against the Buccaneers on Sunday, Oct. 4.

headline: Golden caught four of six targets for 58 yards in Sunday's 20-17 overtime win over the Jets.
story: In addition to leading the team in receiving yards, Golden drew a pivotal 38-yard pass interference penalty to get the Packers out of a first-and-25 hole on a drive that culminated in a Christian Watson touchdown catch to cut the deficit to three points in the fourth quarter. Golden has been out-targeted 19-18 by Watson through two games, and both wide receivers figure to maintain prominent roles in Thursday's Week 3 home game against the Eagles. Fellow Packers wideout Jayden Reed (neck) looks unlikely to suit up for that game after being carted off the field on the opening drive Sunday.

headline: Golden caught six of 12 targets for 95 yards in Sunday's 39-22 loss to the Vikings.
story: With the Packers chasing the Vikings on the scoreboard much of the fourth quarter and getting virtually nothing from their running game all day, Jordan Love dropped back to pass 46 times, and Golden's 40 routes and 12 targets both led the team, as he lined up out wide 92.5 percent of the time. The second-year wideout's 28.6 percent target share is a great sign for his fantasy viability moving forward. Golden will be a WR3 with upside next Sunday on the road against the Jets.

headline: Golden finished the Packers' preseason schedule with one catch (on one target) for 19 yards across two games.
story: Golden was held without a target in the team's exhibition opener but was on the receiving end of a dot from QB Jordan Love in Denver in preseason Week 2, displaying the duo's growing rapport. Green Bay invested a first-round pick in Golden during the 2025 Draft, but a crowded receiving corps capped him to just a 29-361-0 line on 44 targets in 14 regular-season games as a rookie. With Romeo Doubs having moved on to the Patriots in free agency and Dontayvion Wicks getting traded to the Eagles this offseason, the WR options for Love are more clear cut between Christian Watson, Jayden Reed and Golden, giving the latter a better chance to tap into his potential in the upcoming campaign.

headline: Golden secured his only target for 19 yards in the Packers' 33-13 preseason win over the Broncos on Friday.
story: The speedy wideout's one catch was nothing if not noteworthy, as it came on fourth down and against Broncos All-Pro cornerback Patrick Surtain. Golden put together an inconsistent but serviceable 2025 rookie campaign where he generated a 29-361-0 line on 44 targets over 14 regular-season games, but he posted a four-catch, 84-yard, one-touchdown tally in the wild-card loss to the Bears, and he's expected to take on a much bigger role this season following the offseason departures of Romeo Doubs and Dontayvion Wicks.

headline: Is Drake London or Christian Watson a better fantasy option in Week 6?
story: Is Drake London or Christian Watson a better fantasy option in Week 6?

headline: Why Christian Watson is a fantasy must-start
story: Why Christian Watson is a fantasy must-start

headline: Watson brought in six of eight targets for 143 yards and two touchdowns in the Packers' 31-7 win over the Bears on Sunday.
story: Watson tied for the team lead in receptions with Matthew Golden while setting the pace in both receiving yards and targets. Watson struck for the first of his two touchdowns with a 42-yard grab that capped off Green Bay's 10-play opening drive. The veteran field-stretcher then added a spectacular contested 53-yard touchdown reception to put a stamp on the Packers' first drive of the second half, and Watson ultimately finished just five yards short of eclipsing the season-high 147 he put up in Week 1 against the Vikings. Watson will take a 26-474-6 line into a Week 6 home showdown against the Cowboys next Sunday night.

headline: Watson secured all three targets for 47 yards in the Packers' 17-14 win over the Buccaneers on Sunday.
story: Watson led the Packers in receiving yards on an afternoon when Jordan Love threw for only 197 yards. The speedy wideout's reception, receiving yardage and target totals were all season lows, but Watson has still enjoyed a productive start to the campaign with a 20-331-4 line on 32 targets and good health throughout.
